doubles-triples.name: Doubles Triples
doubles-triples.description: Practice tests for the Doubles Triples endorsement

questions.question: You should check the height of the trailer before connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer. The trailer height is right when:
options: The trailer will be raised slightly when the converter dolly is backed under it.
The center of the kingpin lines up with the locking jaws
The kingpin rests on the fifth wheel
questions.explanation: Make sure trailer height is correct. It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so trailer is raised slightly when dolly is pushed under.

questions.question: The best way to stop all skids is to:
questions.explanation: When any vehicle starts to skid, you must act to restore traction to the wheels.

questions.question: When does the drivers manual advise disconnecting the steering axle brakes to help keep the rig straight?
questions.explanation: You should never disconnect the steering axel brakes.

questions.question: When driving with more than one trailer, which trailer should be the first one behind the tractor?
questions.explanation: For the safest handling on the road, the more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in first position behind the tractor. The lighter trailer should be in the rear.

questions.question: Driving a truck with double or triple trailers requires a driver to:
options: Allow more following distance than for smaller vehicles
Use special care in bad weather and mountain conditions
questions.explanation: Be more careful in adverse conditions like bad weather, slippery conditions, and mountain driving, you must be especially careful if you drive double and triple trailers. You will have greater length and more dead axles to pull with your drive axles than other drivers. There is more chance for skids and loss of traction.

questions.question: Which of these will result in the best control on curves?
options: Slowing to a safe speed before entering the curve, then accelerate slightly during the curve
Downshift after you enter the curve
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed, and downshift to the right gear before entering the curve. This lets you use some power through the curve to help the vehicle be more stable while turning.

questions.question: You are driving a 100' vehicle with double trailers at 30 MPH. The road is dry, and visibility is good. You should keep at least _____ seconds of space ahead of you:
questions.explanation: One good rule says you need at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph. At greater speeds, you must add 1 second for safety.

questions.question: You are driving with double trailers and must use your brakes to avoid a crash. For emergency braking you should:
options: Push the brake pedal as hard as you can and hold it there
questions.explanation: You should brake in a way that will keep your vehicle in a straight line and allow you to turn if it becomes necessary. You can use the controlled braking method or the stab braking method.

questions.question: You are doing a walk around inspection of a double or triple trailer rig. You should be sure the converter dolly air tank drain valves are _____ and the pintle hook is _____.
questions.explanation: Converter dolly air tank drain valve are closed, and make sure pintle hook is latched.

questions.question: A converter dolly is
options: an electronic device that connects the electric power from a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer.
a coupling device that connects a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer.
a coupling device that converts the electricity between a semitrailer and a tractor-trailer for international trucking.
questions.explanation: A converter gear on a dolly is a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor trailer combination forming a double bottom rig.

questions.question: If a converter dolly has spring brakes, you release the brakes by
options: using the dolly's parking brake control.
questions.explanation: Release dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock, or, if the dolly has spring brakes, use the dolly parking brake control.

questions.question: You have connected the converter dolly to the front semitrailer and then connected the rear semitrailer to the converter dolly. How should you test the coupling?
options: Pull against the rear semitrailer's pin.
Drive forward, brake suddenly, and see if the rear semitrailer hits the one in front of it.
Drive forward slowly and see if the rear semitrailer stays attached.
questions.explanation: Test coupling by pulling against pin of the rear semitrailer

questions.question: To test the tractor protection valve, charge the trailer air brake system, turn off the engine, and
options: flash your high-beam headlights on and off several times.
keep pressing the brake pedal firmly.
step on and off the brake pedal several times.
questions.explanation: Charge the trailer air brake system. Shut the engine off. Step on and off the brake pedal several times to reduce the air pressure in the tanks. The trailer air supply control should pop out or go from "normal" to "emergency" position when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer. Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.

questions.question: If your landing gear is power operated, you should check for ________ during your walk-around inspection.
options: leaks of air or hydraulic fluid
questions.explanation: If the landing gear is power operated, make sure there are no air or hydraulic leaks.

questions.question: Coupling a triple trailer is different from coupling other combinations because
options: you couple the third trailer to the second trailer before you couple them to the first trailer.
you do not have to use a converter dolly.
you couple the second trailer to the first trailer and then couple them both to the tractor.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle has four units (not counting the converter dollies): a tractor and three trailers. You couple a triple as follows: 1. Couple the first trailer to the tractor the same way that you couple any combination vehicle. 2. Couple the third trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles (which will involve the use of a converter dolly). 3. Move another converter dolly into position. 3. Couple the tractor and first trailer to the second and third trailer using the method for coupling doubles (which will involve another converter dolly).

questions.question: The tractor protection valve is designed to close automatically when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer, typically
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control should pop out or go from "normal" to "emergency" position when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer. Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.

questions.question: In order, the four steps to test your trailer's service brakes are as follows
options: Check for normal air pressure. Release the parking brakes. Pull forward slowly. Apply the trailer brakes, using the hand control if so equipped.
Apply the trailer brakes, using the hand control if so equipped. Release the trailer's parking brakes. Check for normal air pressure. Pull forward slowly.
Check for normal air pressure. Release the parking brakes. Apply the trailer brakes, using the hand control if so equipped. Step off the brakes and pull forward slowly.
questions.explanation: Wait for normal air pressure, release the parking brake, move the vehicle forward slowly about five mph, and apply the brakes firmly using the trailers hand control. Note any vehicle pulling to one side, unusual feel, or delayed stopping action.

questions.question: If your test of the tractor protection valve is successful,
options: the tractor protection valve control (trailer air supply control) will pop out or go from "normal" to "emergency."
the parking brake valve will pop out.
the low air pressure warning signal will come on.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control also called the tractor protection valve control should pop out or go from "normal" to "emergency" position when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.

questions.question: To uncouple the rear trailer, the first thing you do is
options: park the vehicle in a straight line on firm level ground.
park the vehicle at a 45-degree angle on an incline.
park the vehicle at a 45-degree angle on level ground.
questions.explanation: Park rig in a straight line on firm level ground.

questions.question: A converter dolly with antilock brakes (ABS) is required to have
options: a yellow lamp on the left side.
a white lamp on the right side.
a white lamp on the left side.
questions.explanation: Converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to have antilock brakes. These dollies will have a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.

questions.question: You are driving a 100-foot twin trailer combination at 50 mph. The road is dry, and visibility is good. You should keep at least _____ seconds of space ahead of you.
questions.explanation: One good rule says you need at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph. At greater speeds, you must add 1 second for safety.

questions.question: Some large trucks have convex or spot mirrors.
options: Are against the law in most states
Make things look smaller and farther away than the really are
Do not need to be checked as often as flat mirrors because they show a larger area
questions.explanation: The convex mirrors are located below the outside flat mirrors. They are used to monitor the left and right sides at a wide angle. They provide a view of traffic and clearances. These mirrors present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance.

questions.question: Which of these statements about managing space to the sides is true?
options: Always keep your vehicle to the right side of your lane
High winds are not a problem for doubles and triples
You should avoid traveling next to others when possible
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles are often wide and take up most of a lane. Safe drivers will manage what little space they have. You can do this by keeping your vehicle centered in your lane and avoid driving alongside others.

questions.question: Which of these statements about handling of doubles and triples is true?
options: A triple rig can stop quicker than a 5-axle tractor semi-trailer due to off tracking
The rear trailer of a 100-foot triple is less likely to turn over than a single semi-trailer due to the crack the whip effect
A sudden movement with the steering wheel can result in a tipped over rear trailer
questions.explanation: To prevent trailers from rolling over, you must steer gently and go slowly around corners, on ramps, off ramps, and curves. A safe speed on a curve for a straight truck or a single trailer combination vehicle may be too fast for a set of doubles or triples.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors while making a lane change?
options: Right after starting the lane change
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors: Before you change lanes to make sure there is enough room. After you have signaled, to check that no one has moved into your blind spot. Right after you start the lane change, to doublecheck that your path is clear. After you complete the lane change.

questions.question: Before you can supply air to the air tanks of a second trailer you need to:
options: Close the shut off valves at the rear of both trailers
Open the shut off valves at the rear of both trailers
Open the shut off valves at the rear of the first trailer, and close the shut off valves at the rear of the second trailer
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves at rear of trailers, in service and emergency lines. Rear of front trailers: open. Rear of last trailer: closed.

questions.question: If you must drive through deep puddles or flowing water, which of these should you not do?
options: Gently pressing the brake pedal while driving through the water.
questions.explanation: Slow down and place transmission in a low gear. Gently put on the brakes. This presses linings against brake drums or discs and keeps mud, silt, sand, and water from getting in.

questions.question: During an inspection of a double or triple combination, check the usual things for any combination vehicle and check
options: the fifth wheel and the landing gear.
the trailers and the radios in the tractor.
the shut-off valves, the converter dolly or dollies, and the air brakes on all trailers.
questions.explanation: To inspect a double or triple, first inspect it just as you would inspect any combination vehicle. Then check that the shut-off valves are open on all trailers but the last trailer. Check each converter dolly to be sure that the pintle hook is properly latched.

questions.question: When you pull two or three trailers, you should look farther ahead because
options: aggressive drivers may cause trouble for you on the road.
the vehicle is more likely to roll over or jackknife.
both of the above are true.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples must be driven very smoothly to avoid rollover or jackknife. Therefore, look far ahead so you can slow down or change lanes gradually when necessary.

questions.question: If you want to couple a second trailer to your combination vehicle, secure it by using?
options: The trailers spring brakes and emergency air brakes
questions.explanation: Make sure trailer brakes are locked and/or wheels chocked.

questions.question: Which of these statements about quick steering movements and doubles / triples is true?
options: Doubles / triples flip over from quick steering movement easier than many other vehicles
You should put on the brakes at the same time you perform quick steering movements
Counter steering is easier with doubles / triples than with most other vehicles
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification causes the crack-the-whip effect. Triples have a rearward amplification of 3.5 meaning you can roll the last trailer of triples 3.5 times as easily as a five-axle tractor. A Double has a reward amplification of 2 being twice as likely to roll over as a five-axel trailer.

questions.question: The best way to keep brakes from overheating while going down a steep grade is to:
options: Go 5 MPH below your safe speed
questions.explanation: The use of brakes on a long and/or steep downgrade is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine. The following are the proper braking techniques: Apply the brakes just hard enough to feel a definite slowdown. When your speed has been reduced to approximately five mph below your "safe" speed, release the brakes. When your speed has increased to your "safe" speed, repeat.

questions.question: Converter dollies:
options: Often do not have spring brakes
Have little braking power because they are small
Usually need a glad hand converter
questions.explanation: Converter dollies often do not have spring brakes.

questions.question: You are driving a set of doubles, and a set of trailer wheels goes into a skid. Which of these is most likely to occur?
options: The rig will continue to move in a straight line no matter how much the steering wheel is turned
The rig will stay in a straight line but slide sideways
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples must be driven very smoothly to avoid rollover or jackknife. Therefore, look far ahead so you can slow down or change lanes gradually when necessary.

questions.question: Antilock brakes (ABS) have been required on all converter dollies built since
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 require ABS, and other air brake vehicles such as trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 require ABS.

questions.question: Why must you inspect your double or triple combination vehicle more extensively than a vehicle with only one such semitrailer?
options: Its design makes it more likely to have problems.
There are more critical parts to check.
The types of cargoes it carries make it more likely to have problems.
questions.explanation: There are more things to inspect on a double or triple combination vehicle than on a single vehicle. Many of these items are simply more of what you would find on a single vehicle. For example, tires, wheels, lights, reflectors, etc. However, there are also some new things to check.

questions.question: Which of these statements about seeing ahead is true?
options: At highway speed you should look up to 1/4 mile ahead of your truck
Good drivers shift their attention back and forth, near and far
Many drivers do not look far enough ahead of their truck
questions.explanation: Most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead. That means looking ahead the distance you will travel in 12 to 15 seconds. At lower speeds, that's about one block. At highway speeds it's about a quarter of a mile.

questions.question: The crack the whip effects trucks with trailers. Which of the following is most likely to tip over?
options: The rear trailer of a triple
The rear trailer of a double
A full trailer behind a truck
questions.explanation: Due to rearward amplification a double is twice as likely, and a triple is 3.5 times more likely to roll over than a five-axel trailer.

questions.question: A converter dolly consists of a ______ wheel and ________ axles.
questions.explanation: A converter gear on a dolly is a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor trailer combination forming a double bottom rig.

questions.question: The first step in uncoupling a converter dolly is
options: to slowly pull clear of it.
questions.explanation: Lower dolly landing gear.

questions.question: How can you be sure you supplied air to a second trailer?
options: Go to the rear of the second trailer and open the emergency line shut off
Watch each trailers air gauge for a drop of 30 PSI
Apply the hand valve at 10 MPH, you should stop in the same distance as a truck with one trailer at 5 MPH
questions.explanation: Use the tractor parking brake and/or chock the wheels to hold the vehicle. Wait for air pressure to reach normal, then push in the red "trailer air supply" knob. This will supply air to the emergency (supply) lines. Open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer. You should hear air escaping, showing the entire system is charged.

questions.question: If a converter dolly is still under the second trailer and you unlock the pintle hook, what will probably happen?
options: The dolly tow bar may fly up
questions.explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer. The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury, and making it very difficult to re-couple.

questions.question: You are visually checking the coupling of a converter dolly to the rear trailer. How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.explanation: Check that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap.

questions.question: When you uncouple twin trailers, the last step is to
options: release the brakes on the converter dolly.
slowly pull clear of the converter dolly.
questions.explanation: Slowly pull clear of dolly.

questions.question: Converter dollies
options: have little braking power because they are small.
sometimes do not have antilock brakes.
usually need a glad hand converter.
questions.explanation: All converter dollies built since 1998 are required to have antilock brakes.

questions.question: You want to hook your combination to a second trailer that has no spring brakes. To do this without wheel chocks you should:
options: Supply air to the trailer air system with the tractor and then disconnect the emergency line
Make sure the trailer will roll freely when coupling
Hook the trailer electric cord to a portable generator for braking power
questions.explanation: If the second trailer doesn't have spring brakes, drive the tractor close to the trailer, connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, and disconnect the emergency line. This will set the trailer emergency brakes if the slack adjusters are correctly adjusted.

questions.question: Empty trucks:
options: Require shorter stopping distances than full ones.
May have poor traction due to bouncing and wheel lockup
Are the easiest to stop since there is no shifting cargo
questions.explanation: Empty trucks require greater stopping distances because an empty vehicle has less traction.

questions.question: When parking your double or triple combination, you should look for a parking space
options: that you can pull straight through.
that is as close as possible to your destination.
that you can back out of.
questions.explanation: Make sure you do not get in a spot you cannot pull straight through. You need to be aware of how parking lots are arranged to avoid a long and difficult escape.

questions.question: With the hand valve on, you should test the trailer brakes by opening the service line valve at the rear of the rig. When you do this, you should hear:
options: The emergency line valve open and release air
The service brakes slowly move to the fully applied position
Air escapes from the open valve
questions.explanation: Open the service line valve, listen for air to escape, and then close the valve.

questions.question: Which of these in not a good thing to do when driving on slippery roads?
options: Use the engine brake or speed retarder
Keep other traffic out of you side space
Use a light touch on the accelerator and brake pedals
questions.explanation: When your drive wheels have poor traction, the retarder may cause them to skid. Therefore, you should turn the retarder off whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered.

questions.question: Double and triple combination vehicles are ________ stable than other types of commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Take special care when pulling two and three trailers. There are more things that can go wrong, and doubles/triples are less stable than other commercial vehicles.

hazardous-material.name: Hazardous Material
hazardous-material.description: Practice tests for the Hazardous Material endorsement

questions.question: How many different hazard classes are there?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are categorized into nine major hazard classes and additional categories for consumer commodities and combustible liquids.

questions.question: What placard must be used with an inhalation hazard load?
questions.explanation: If the words inhalation hazard appear on the shipping paper or package, the rules require display of the poison inhalation hazard or poison gas placards, as appropriate.

questions.question: A truck carrying explosives has crashed with another vehicle. You should not pull them apart until?
options: The shipper's loading foreman is present
The explosives have been placed at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and occupied buildings
questions.explanation: Remove all explosives before separating vehicles involved in a collision. Place the explosives at least 200 feet from the vehicles and occupied buildings. Stay a safe distance away.

questions.question: The shippers' package hazardous materials, they must certify that this was done according to the regulations. The only exception is when:
options: The shipper is a private carrier carrying his or her own product
The shipment is a hazardous waste
The driver is given a sealed cargo compartment
questions.explanation: The signed shipper's certification appears on the original shipping paper. The only exceptions are when a shipper is a private carrier transporting their own product and when the package is provided by the carrier.

questions.question: Which signals may be used to warn of a stopped vehicle that contains explosives?
questions.explanation: You might break down and have to use stopped vehicle signals. Use reflective triangles or red electric lights, never use burning signals, such as flares or fuses around a tank used for Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) or Division 2.1 (Flammable Gas) whether loaded or empty, and any vehicle loaded with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 Explosives.

questions.question: Class 8 is placarded as?
options: A placard blasting agent at any amount
questions.explanation: Class 8 - Corrosive Materials.

questions.question: The transport index of a radioactive material:
options: Is another way of writing the weight of the package.
Tells the degree of control needed during transportation
Is something that only the shipper needs to worry about
questions.explanation: Radiation surrounds each package, passing through all nearby packages. To deal with this problem, the number of packages you can load together is controlled. Their closeness to people, animals, and unexposed film is also controlled. The transport index tells the degree of control needed during transportation.

questions.question: A properly prepared uniform hazardous waste manifest:
options: Must be signed and carried by anyone transporting a hazardous waste
Is the same as any other shipping paper
Is required only if there is a loss of cargo during transport
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous wastes, you must sign by hand and carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest

questions.question: An "A or W" the first column of the hazardous materials table means:
options: It is ok to ship this material by air only
There are no restrictions with this material if shipped by water only
This material has no restrictions when shipped by air and/or water
This material is only restricted when shipped by air and/or water
questions.explanation: Means the hazardous material described in Column 2 is subject to the HMR only when offered or intended for transport by air and/or water unless it is a hazardous substance or hazardous waste.

questions.question: When is it necessary to ground the trailer?
options: Only when filling a trailer with explosives
Only when unloading a cargo tank filled with any flammable liquid
When filling or unloading any flammable liquid tank, ground must be maintained until filling hole is properly closed
questions.explanation: Ground a cargo tank correctly before filling it through an open filling hole. Ground the tank before opening the filling hole and maintain the ground until after closing the filling hole.

questions.question: The total transport index of all radioactive material packages in a single vehicle must not exceed _____.
questions.explanation: The total transport index of all packages in a single vehicle must not exceed 50.

questions.question: Which of the following must drivers have in their possession while transporting class 1.1 or 1.3 explosives?
questions.explanation: If transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, you must have a written route plan and follow that plan. Carriers prepare the route plan in advance and give the driver a copy

questions.question: On a public roadway with a placarded tanker hauling flammable liquids, when can you transfer from one tanker to another?
options: When the fire department is there
You should never make a transfer
questions.explanation: Don't transfer flammable liquid from one vehicle to another on a public roadway except in an emergency.

questions.question: If in a materials class is the word "forbidden", what kinds of materials are you still allowed to haul?
options: You can't haul a forbidden cargo
questions.explanation: Column 3 shows a material's hazard class or division, or the entry "Forbidden." Never transport a "Forbidden" material.

questions.question: What is the shape and size of a placard?
options: at least a 250 mm square or diamond
questions.explanation: Placards must be readable from all four directions. They must be at least 250 mm square, turned upright on a point, in a diamond shape.

questions.question: When handling packages of explosives, you must:
options: Never use hooks or other metal tools
Double wrap wet boxes in plastic to prevent staining
questions.explanation: Use extra care to protect explosives. Never use hooks or other metal tools. Never drop, throw, or roll packages. Protect explosive packages from other cargo that might cause damage

questions.question: Which of the following, if required, must the shipper put on the package.
options: The name and address of shipper or co-signee
The hazardous materials shipping name and identification number
questions.explanation: Shippers print required markings directly on the package, an attached label, or tag. When required, the shipper will put the following on the package: the name and address of shipper or consignee, the hazardous material's shipping name and identification number, and the labels required.

questions.question: Whenever your vehicle is placarded, do not drive near open fires unless you:
options: Have legal total limit of a nonflammable material
Can safely pass the fire without stopping
questions.explanation: Never drive a placarded vehicle near open fires unless you can safely pass without stopping.

questions.question: A hazard class name or ID number may not be used to describe a:
options: Reportable quantity of a hazardous substance
questions.explanation: A hazard class name or ID number may not be used to describe non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: Column 1 or the symbols column the "I" means:
questions.explanation: Identifies a proper shipping name that is used to describe materials in international transportation. A different shipping name may be used when only domestic transportation is involved.

questions.question: What action should you take if you discover your hazardous materials shipment leaking at a rest stop but there is no phone available?
options: Keep driving slowly and cautiously until you reach a phone.
Send someone for help with all the necessary information.
Keep driving for help as quickly as possible.
Leave your truck parked with its emergency lights on and walk for help.
questions.explanation: Never continue driving with hazardous materials leaking from your vehicle in order to find a phone booth, truck stop, help, or similar reason. If hazardous materials are spilling from your vehicle: Park it, secure the area, stay there, send someone else for help.

questions.question: In what location must you keep your shipping papers that describe any hazardous materials?
options: On the driver's seat whenever you are out of the vehicle
In a fireproof pouch under the passenger seat while you are driving
In a locked glove compartment whenever you are out of the vehicle
In a fireproof pouch under the driver's seat that you can reach while you are driving
questions.explanation: You must identify shipping papers related to hazardous materials or keep them on top of other shipping papers. You must also keep shipping papers: In a pouch on the driver's door, or in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.

questions.question: You must never smoke or perform any activity involving fire within 25 feet of
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank used for Class 3 (flammable liquids),Division 2.1 (gases), or Class 1 (Explosives) Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) Class 4 (Flammable Solids) Class 4.2 (Spontaneously Combustible). Oxidizers fall under flammable solids.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a driver placarding their vehicle?
options: To give people something interesting to look at while they drive
To warn those with children to drive in another lane
To force other drivers to stay 20 feet away in every direction
questions.explanation: The three intents are: Contain the Material; Communicate the Risk; and Assure Safe Drivers and Equipment.

questions.question: If you are already carrying 100 pounds of silver cyanide, what precautions must you take if you are given papers at a dock to carry 100 cartons of battery acid?
options: Inform someone and do not load the battery acid.
Make sure the battery acid is loaded on top of the silver cyanide.
Make sure the silver cyanide is loaded on top of the battery acid.
Make sure there is plenty of space between the two.
questions.explanation: Acids, corrosive materials, or other acidic materials which could release hydrocyanic acid. For Example: Cyanides, Inorganic, Silver Cyanide, or Sodium Cyanide.

questions.question: The other two places where the hazardous material identification number must appear are
options: on a temporary license plate holder and on the steering wheel.
on the back of the truck and inside the glove compartment.
on all bulk packaging and on the cargo tanks.
on the gas tank and on a sticker in the glove compartment.
questions.explanation: In addition to the two main locations for the hazardous material identification number, you must also display it on the cargo tanks and on all bulk packaging.

questions.question: When there is a hazardous materials emergency, what should you do?
options: Prevent smoking and keep open flames away.
Keep people away and warn them of danger.
questions.explanation: Follow this checklist: Check to see that your driving partner is OK, keep shipping papers with you, keep people far away and upwind, warn others of the danger, and call for help.

questions.question: Whose signatures must be on a Hazardous Waste Manifest?
options: The shipper, all carriers, and the receiver
The shipper and the first carrier
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous wastes, you must sign by hand and carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. Shippers must prepare, date, and sign by hand the manifest. Each carrier transporting the shipment must sign by hand the manifest. Each copy must have all needed signatures and dates, including those of the person to whom you delivered the waste.

questions.question: To obtain a hazardous materials endorsement, you must know how to
options: package different types of hazardous materials for transport.
identify various types of hazardous materials by smell and appearance.
questions.explanation: The hazardous materials test required if you want to haul hazardous materials as defined in 49 CFR 383.5. In order to obtain this endorsement, you are also required to pass a Transportation Security Administration (TSA) background check.

questions.question: A shipping paper for hazardous materials must include
options: page numbers if the shipping paper has more than one page.
a proper shipping description for each hazardous material and a shipper's certification stating that they prepared the shipment according to the regulations.
questions.explanation: A shipping paper for hazardous materials must include: Page numbers if the shipping paper has more than one page, a proper shipping description for each hazardous material, and shipper's certification signed by the shipper saying they prepared the shipment according to the regulations.

questions.question: The driver must always also carry on his person a dated certificate signed by the employer. This certificate must also be updated every
questions.explanation: The regulations require that hazardous materials employees be trained and tested at least once every three years

questions.question: If an X or RQ is in the HM column of a shipping paper entry, the:
options: Material listed on that line in the largest part of the shipment
Entry refers to the materials that must be top loaded
Shipment is regulated by hazardous material regulations
questions.explanation: If a shipping paper describes both hazardous and non-hazardous products, the hazardous materials must be: Entered first. Highlighted in a contrasting color or identified by an "X" placed before the shipping description in a column captioned "HM". The letters "RQ" may be used instead of "X" if a reportable quantity needs to be identified.

questions.question: When there is a hazardous materials emergency. You should:
options: Keep people away and warn them of the danger
Prevent smoking and keep open flames away
questions.explanation: Follow this checklist: Check to see that your driving partner is OK, keep the shipping papers with you, keep people far away and upwind, warn others of the danger, and call for help.

questions.question: The placard is shaped?
questions.explanation: Placards must be readable from all four directions. They must be at least 10 3/4 inches square, turned upright on a point, in a diamond shape.

questions.question: Which of the following choices is a hazard class you are not allowed to smoke around?
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank used for Class 3 (flammable liquids),Division 2.1 (gases), or Class 1 (Explosives) Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) Class 4 (Flammable Solids) Class 4.2 (Spontaneously Combustible). Oxidizers fall under flammable solids.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the three keys to identify which placard to use?
questions.explanation: The three keys are: Materials Hazard Class, Amount Being Shipped, and amount of all Hazardous materials of all classes on your vehicle.

questions.question: If there is an "RQ" before or after the item description on the shipping paper, it means the:
options: Material has an insurance value of over $1,000
Material is in a package containing no other materials
Carrier must report any spill of this material
questions.explanation: The letters RQ may appear before or after the basic description. You or your employer must report any spill of these materials, which occurs in a reportable quantity.

questions.question: Symbol column, the letter "G" stands for?
options: Identifies the proper shipping name for which one or more technical names of the hazardous material must be entered in parentheses, along with the basic description
questions.explanation: Means this hazardous material described in Column 2 is a generic shipping name. A generic shipping name must be accompanied by a technical name on the shipping paper.

questions.question: Drivers of placarded vehicles transporting hazardous materials must stop _____ to _____ feet from the nearest rail of a railroad.
questions.explanation: You must stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail. Proceed only when you are sure no train is coming, and you can clear the tracks without stopping. Don't shift gears while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: Carriers must give each driver who transports class 1.1 or 1.3 explosives:
questions.explanation: A carrier must give each driver transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives a copy of Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSR), Part 397.

questions.question: Animals and human foodstuffs should not be loaded in the same vehicle with?
questions.explanation: Poison or poison inhalation hazard labeled material should not be loaded with animal or human food unless the poison package is over packed in an approved way.

questions.question: A safe haven is one place you can leave a vehicle unattended that is hauling explosives. What is the best description of a safe haven?
options: Any property that is totally fenced in by an 8-foot-high fence
Any property that is totally fenced in by an 8-foot-high fence and has a guard on duty all day long
Any property that has been government approved for this use
questions.explanation: A safe haven is an approved place for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives. Designation of authorized safe havens is usually made by local authorities.

questions.question: Who is responsible for finding out what permits or special routes you will need to haul hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The driver makes sure the shipper has identified, marked, and labeled the hazardous materials properly. Refuses leaking packages and shipments. Placards vehicle when loading, if required. Safely transports the shipment without delay. Follows all special rules about transporting hazardous materials. Keeps hazardous materials shipping papers and emergency.

questions.question: You do not have a hazardous materials endorsement on your commercial driver license. When can you legally haul hazardous materials?
options: Only when the load is placarded
Only when the shipment does not cross state lines
questions.explanation: The rules require all drivers of placarded vehicles to learn how to safely load and transport hazardous products. They must have a commercial driver license with the hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: Nitric acid cannot be loaded:
questions.explanation: Do not load nitric acid above any other product.

questions.question: When shippers package the material, they are trying to
options: make it easy to open and close the packages.
make it as light as possible.
questions.explanation: The shipper must package, mark, and label the materials; prepare shipping papers; provide emergency response information; and supply placards. Making the load easy to identify.

questions.question: To determine if you need to use placards, which of the following is NOT something you need to know?
options: The amount of a substance or material being shipped
The amount of all the hazardous materials of all classes in your vehicle
The manufacturing date of the material
The hazard class of the substance or material
questions.explanation: To decide which placards to use, you need to know: The hazard class of the materials, the amount of hazardous materials shipped the total weight of all classes of hazardous materials in your vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an acceptable type of marking for hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Names shown in italics are not proper shipping names and not acceptable, those in roman type above it are.

questions.question: Which of the following three hazard classes should NOT be placed into a temperature-controlled trailer (one with a heater or air conditioner unit)?
questions.explanation: The three hazard classes that must be kept in a trailer without automatic heating and cooling are: explosives (1), flammable gases (2.1), and flammable liquids (3), because these are particularly volatile.

questions.question: What are the major differences between cargo tanks and portable tanks?
options: Cargo tanks are filled while on the vehicle; portable tanks can be filled either on or off the vehicle.
Cargo tanks are permanently attached to vehicles; portable tanks are temporarily attached.
Portable tanks must show the owner or lessee's name on them.
All of the above are major differences.
questions.explanation: Cargo tanks are bulk packaging permanently attached to a vehicle. Cargo tanks remain on the vehicle when you load and unload them. Portable tanks are bulk packaging, which are not permanently attached to a vehicle.

questions.question: The Hazardous Materials Table has ______ columns.
questions.explanation: The Hazardous Materials Table lists every type of material that the US Department of Transportation has designated as a hazardous material for the purpose of transportation. There are eight columns in the Hazardous Materials Table, describing the mode of transportation (air, ground, water, etc.), the name of the material, its hazard class, its identification number, and so on.

questions.question: To communicate the risk of hazardous materials, shippers do all of the following EXCEPT
options: have their drivers text their locations.
questions.explanation: To communicate the risk of hazardous materials, regulations require shippers to put placards on trucks, put hazard warning labels on packages, provide proper shipping papers, and supply emergency response information.

questions.question: A hazardous material's identification number is determined by
questions.explanation: The shipper uses the hazardous materials regulations to determine the product's: Identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class, packing group, correct packaging, correct label and markings, and correct placards.

questions.question: You have loaded a hazardous material into a cargo tank. What must you do before you move the vehicle?
options: Close all manholes and valves. Be sure they are free of leaks.
Call CHEMTREC by phone and tell them where you are going.
Have the loading observers sign the shipping papers.
questions.explanation: Close all manholes and valves before moving a tank of hazardous materials, no matter how small the amount in the tank or how short the distance.

questions.question: You have a vehicle without racks to hold cylinders or compressed gas. You may load such cylinders only if they are
options: less than half of the load.
bundled loosely together with steel strapping.
loaded upright or lying down flat and braced.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle doesn't have racks to hold cylinders, the cargo space floor must be flat. The cylinders must be: Held upright, in racks attached to the vehicle or in boxes that will keep them from turning over and may be loaded in a horizontal position if it is designed so the relief valve is in the vapor space.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine in cargo tanks, what must you have?
options: An emergency kit for controlling leaks in fittings on the dome cover plate
questions.explanation: A driver transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must have an approved gas mask in the vehicle. The driver must also have an emergency kit for controlling leaks in dome cover plate fittings on the cargo tank.

questions.question: When can the shipping name or the hazardous material identification number be abbreviated on the shipping paper?
options: Only if regulations specifically authorize the shipper to do it
Only if there isn't enough room for the whole thing
Only if it is one of the five most frequently shipped hazardous materials
questions.explanation: Identification number, shipping name, and hazard class must not be abbreviated unless specifically authorized in the hazardous materials regulations

questions.question: Your engine runs a pump when you are delivering compressed gas. After finishing the delivery, when should you turn off the engine?
options: Leave it on the entire time.
Turn it off on arrival; use other power to run the pump.
Turn it off after unhooking the hoses.
Turn it off before unhooking the hoses.
questions.explanation: Unless your engine runs a pump for product transfer, turn it off when loading or unloading. If you use the engine, turn it off after product transfer, before you unhook the hose.

questions.question: Which of the following materials are acceptable floor liners for transporting Division 1.1 or 1.2 materials?
questions.explanation: Use a floor lining with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3. The floors must be tight, and the liner must be either nonmetallic material or non-ferrous metal.

questions.question: Where are the two main places that the hazardous material identification number appears?
options: On the packages and on paperwork at the shipping point of origin
On the packages and on paperwork at the shipping destination
On the shipping papers and on a secret document in the driver's wallet
On the shipping papers and on the packages
questions.explanation: Always make sure that the shipper shows the correct basic description on the shipping paper and verifies that the proper labels are shown on the packages.

questions.question: You can't haul 1.1 explosives with?
questions.explanation: Do not transport Division 1.1 or 1.2 in vehicle combinations if: There is a marked or placarded cargo tank in the combination. The other vehicle in the combination contains: Division 1.1 A (Initiating Explosives). Packages of Class 7 (Radioactive) materials labeled "Yellow III." Division 2.3 (Poisonous Gas) or Division 6.1 (Poisonous) materials. Hazardous materials in a portable tank, on a DOT Spec 106A or 110A tank.

questions.question: When fueling a placarded vehicle, someone must always be:
options: Within 10 feet of the pump with a fire extinguisher
At the nozzle, controlling the fuel flow
At the emergency power shut off for the pump
questions.explanation: Turn off your engine before fueling a motor vehicle containing hazardous materials. Someone must always be at the nozzle, controlling fuel flow.

questions.question: What is Chemtrec's primary job?
options: They maintain the scene and keep people away
They coordinate and advise companies on spills; they also link up proper authorities with those companies
questions.explanation: The Chemical Transportation Emergency Center (CHEMTREC) in Washington also has a 24-hour toll-free line. CHEMTREC was created to provide emergency personnel with technical information about the physical properties of hazardous materials.

questions.question: How many identical placards is a vehicle hauling hazardous materials required to display and where?
options: Four, two on the front and two on the back
Two, one on the front and one on the back
Four, one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side of the vehicle
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards. They are put on the front, rear, and both sides.

questions.question: With most hazardous materials, you may park within 5 feet of the road briefly, if your work requires it. The materials that are the exception and do not allow parking this close to the road are?
questions.explanation: Never park with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within five feet of the traveled part of the road.

questions.question: Who is responsible for checking to be sure the shipper correctly named, labeled, and marked a hazardous materials shipment?
questions.explanation: The carrier prior to transportation, checks that the shipper correctly described, marked, labeled, and otherwise prepared the shipment for transportation.

questions.question: There are three lists that drivers, shippers and carriers use to find out if a material is regulated as hazardous. Which one of these choices is not one of those three lists?
options: List of hazardous substances and reportable quantities
questions.explanation: There are three main lists used by shippers, carriers, and drivers when trying to identify hazardous materials. Hazardous Materials Table, List of Hazardous Substances and Reportable Quantities, List of Marine Pollutants.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safely transporting a hazardous material shipment without delay and keeping the shipping papers in the right place?
questions.explanation: The driver cakes sure the shipper has identified, marked, and labeled the hazardous materials properly. Refuses leaking packages and shipments. Placards vehicle when loading, if required. Safely transports the shipment without delay. Follows all special rules about transporting hazardous materials. Keeps hazardous materials shipping papers and emergency

questions.question: When a spill occurs of an "RQ" substance the carrier has within _____ to report the spill.
questions.explanation: Carriers must make detailed written reports within 30 days of an incident

questions.question: You are going to be hauling hazardous materials over a route you do not know well. When should you check the route and get the permits needed for the trip:
options: Within the first 50 miles of the trip
While you are still on a part of the route that you know
questions.explanation: It is your job as driver to find out if you need permits or must use special routes. Make sure you have all needed papers before starting.

questions.question: A placard is required for a combustible liquid at?
questions.explanation: The tank vehicle test required if you want to haul any liquid or gaseous materials in a tank or tanks having an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons.

questions.question: Column 1 or the symbols column the "D" sign means:
questions.explanation: Means the proper shipping name is appropriate for describing materials for domestic transportation but may not be proper for international transportation.

questions.question: What is a technical name?
options: The medical term for hazardous materials used by medical personnel
The name of a hazardous material most commonly used on the street
The name of a hazardous material most commonly used in the trucking community and accepted as standard
The name of a hazardous material used in scientific journals and texts, recognized as its chemical or microbiological name
questions.explanation: A technical name is a specific chemical that makes the product hazardous

questions.question: Which of the following hazard classes uses a transport index to determine how much of it can be loaded on a single vehicle for transport?
questions.explanation: Some packages of Class 7 (Radioactive) materials bear a number called the "transport index." The shipper labels these packages Radioactive II or Radioactive III and prints the package's transport index on the label.

questions.question: Which of the following are necessary qualifications for non-bulk packaging?
options: A maximum net mass of 400 kg (882 pounds) or less and a maximum capacity of 450 L (119 gallons) or less if used as a receptacle for a solid
A water capacity of 454 kg (1,000 pounds) or less if used as a receptacle for a gas
A maximum capacity of 450 L (119 gallons) or less if used as a receptacle for a liquid
questions.explanation: Non-bulk packaging: A maximum capacity of 450 L (119 gallons) as a receptacle for a liquid; A maximum net mass less than 400 kg (882 pounds) and a maximum capacity of 450 L (119 gallons) or less as a receptacle for a solid; or A water capacity greater than 454 kg (1,000 pounds) or less as a receptacle for a gas.

questions.question: Why does the government regulate the transportation of hazardous materials?
options: Because while being transported, they pose a risk to health, property, or safety
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation. Hazardous materials include explosives, various types of gas, solids, flammable and combustible liquid, and other materials. Because of the risks involved and the potential consequences these risks impose, all levels of government regulate the handling of hazardous materials.

questions.question: A properly prepared uniform hazardous waste manifest
options: is required only if there is a loss of cargo during transport.
is the same as any other shipping paper.
must be signed by each carrier transporting the shipment.
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous wastes, you must sign by hand and carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. Shippers must prepare, date, and sign by hand the manifest. Each carrier transporting the shipment must sign by hand the manifest. Each copy must have all needed signatures and dates, including those of the person to whom you delivered the waste.

questions.question: Identification numbers are preceded by the letters "UN" or "NA." The letters "NA" are associated with proper shipping names that are used where?
options: Within the United States and to and from Canada
questions.explanation: The letters "NA" are associated with proper shipping names that are only used within the United States and to and from Canada

questions.question: You may not park a vehicle carrying hazardous materials within _____ feet of an open fire.
questions.explanation: Do not park within 300 feet of: A bridge, tunnel, building, a place where people gather, or an open fire. If you must park to do your job, do so only briefly.

questions.question: What type fire extinguisher is required in the power unit of a placarded vehicle?
options: A UL rating of 10 BC or above
A UL rating of 5 BC or above
questions.explanation: The power unit of placarded vehicles must have a fire extinguisher with a UL rating of 10 B:C or more.

questions.question: To find out if a shipment includes a hazardous material, you should:
options: Open and inspect every package and container
Check for a fence around the loading dock
questions.explanation: Learn to recognize shipments of hazardous materials. To find out if the shipment includes hazardous materials, look at the shipping paper.

questions.question: Cylinders containing compressed gases may only be loaded onto a vehicle without a flat floor or platform if the cylinders are:
options: Loaded in an upright or horizontal position
Loaded into racks attached to the vehicle
In boxes that will keep them from turning over
questions.explanation: The cylinders must be: Held upright, or in racks attached to the vehicle

questions.question: You are hauling hazardous materials and you find that one of your tires is leaking. You must:
options: Continue at reduced speed and check that tire every 25 miles
Stop at the nearest safe place and fix it
Report it to your carrier immediately
questions.explanation: Do not drive with a tire that is leaking or flat except to the nearest safe place to fix it.

questions.question: Shipping papers must always be kept in one place when driving with hazardous materials. Where when wearing your seat belt?
options: In a pouch on the driver's door
questions.explanation: Drivers are to keep hazardous materials shipping papers: In a pouch on the driver's door, or in clear view within immediate reach while the seat belt is fastened while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.

questions.question: You have loaded a hazardous material into a cargo tank. What must you do before you move the vehicle?
options: Call chemtrec by phone and tell them where you are going
Have the loading observers sign the shipping papers
Close all manholes and valves, be sure they are free of leaks
questions.explanation: Close all manholes and valves before moving a tank of hazardous materials, no matter how small the amount in the tank or how short the distance.

questions.question: The hazardous material identification numbers must be displayed on portable tanks, cargo tanks, and other bulk packaging. The regulations require black _______ numbers.
questions.explanation: The rules require black 100 mm (3.9 inch) numbers on orange panels, placards, or a white, diamond-shaped background if no placards are required.

questions.question: The Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG)
options: contains an index of hazardous material identification numbers (which is why you must label things correctly).
was created by the US Department of Transportation and is used nationwide.
is studied by emergency personnel to help keep the public safe.
questions.explanation: The Department of Transportation has a guidebook for firefighters, police, and industry workers on how to protect themselves and the public from hazardous materials. The guide is indexed by proper shipping name and hazardous materials identification number. Emergency personnel look for these things on the shipping paper. That is why it is vital that the proper shipping name, identification number, label, and placards are correct.

questions.question: You should stop before crossing a railroad grade if your vehicle is carrying _______ of chlorine.
questions.explanation: Stop before a railroad crossing if your vehicle: Is placarded, carries any amount of chlorine, has cargo tanks, whether loaded or empty used for hazardous materials.

questions.question: If you are in an accident involving hazardous materials, you should:
options: Tell only the emergency response team about the hazard
Keep all people far away and upwind of the accident
Prevent a panic by acting like nothing is wrong
questions.explanation: As a professional driver, your job at the scene of a crash or an incident is to: Keep people away. Limit the spread of material, if you can safely do so. Communicate the danger of the hazardous materials Provide emergency responders with the shipping papers and emergency response information.

questions.question: It is recommended that when hauling a load of explosives 1.1 or 1.3 to use the fusees instead of the warning triangles if in an emergency or breakdown situation?
questions.explanation: You might break down and have to use stopped vehicle signals. Use reflective triangles or red electric lights, never use burning signals, such as flares or fuses around a tank used for Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) or Division 2.1 (Flammable Gas) whether loaded or empty, and any vehicle loaded with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 Explosives.

questions.question: Who is responsible for packaging, labeling, and preparing the hazardous material shipping papers for a common carrier?
questions.explanation: Must package, mark, and label the materials; prepare shipping papers; provide emergency response information; and supply placards.

questions.question: Class 1.1 explosives must not be transported in a combination vehicle if the vehicle includes:
questions.explanation: Do not transport Division 1.1 or 1.2 in vehicle combinations if: There is a marked or placarded cargo tank in the combination. The other vehicle in the combination contains: Division 1.1 A (Initiating Explosives). Packages of Class 7 (Radioactive) materials labeled "Yellow III." Division 2.3 (Poisonous Gas) or Division 6.1 (Poisonous) materials. Hazardous materials in a portable tank, on a DOT Spec 106A or 110A tank.

questions.question: A vehicle contains 500 pounds each of explosives 1.1 and 1.3, you must use:
questions.explanation: Use the larger or more dangerous placard of explosives 1.1.

questions.question: A railroad crossing is ahead of you and you are hauling hazardous material. When you stop for the crossing, you can stop as far away as _____ feet from the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: You must stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail. Proceed only when you are sure no train is coming, and you can clear the tracks without stopping. Don't shift gears while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: The hazardous waste manifest should be?
options: The same as all other paper work
Tabbed differently and kept on top of all other paperwork
questions.explanation: Hazardous waste need to be kept on top of all other paperwork and tabbed differently so that it is easy to find.

questions.question: Column 1 or the symbols column the "+" sign means:
options: The proper shipping name is invalid
The proper shipping name without regard whether the material meets the definition of that class
Do not use proper shipping name
questions.explanation: The "+" sign shows the proper shipping name, hazard class, and packing group to use, even if the material doesn't meet the hazard class definition

questions.question: How often should you check the tires on a placarded trailer that has dual tires?
options: At the start of each trip and every time you stop
questions.explanation: Check the tire mounting and air pressure. Inspect the tires every two hours, every 100 miles, and each time you stop.

questions.question: Whenever you load or unload a cargo tank, a qualified person must be
questions.explanation: The person in charge of loading and unloading a cargo tank must be sure a qualified person is always watching. This person watching the loading or unloading must: Be alert, have a clear view of the cargo tank, be within 25 feet of the tank, know of the hazards of the materials involved, know the procedures to follow in an emergency, and be authorized to move the cargo tank and able to do so.

questions.question: Containment rules specify
options: how to package, load, transport, and unload hazardous materials safely.
how to safely contain a spill of hazardous materials.
how to drive safely with hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Many hazardous products can injure or kill on contact. To protect drivers and others from contact, the rules tell shippers how to package safely. Similar rules tell drivers how to load, transport, and unload bulk tanks. These are containment rules.

questions.question: Smoking must be at least _____ feet from most hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank used for Class 3 (flammable liquids),Division 2.1 (gases), or Class 1 (Explosives) Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) Class 4 (Flammable Solids) Class 4.2 (Spontaneously Combustible).

questions.question: In the hazardous material table, column 3, any shipping name written in italics means?
options: It isn't the proper shipping name, those in roman type above it are
Just another way of writing the shipping name
That this substance is highly flammable
questions.explanation: Names shown in italics are not proper shipping names, those in roman type above it are.

questions.question: If hazardous material is spilling from your vehicle, do not move your vehicle:
questions.explanation: If hazardous materials are spilling from your vehicle, do not move it any more than safety requires.

questions.question: How often must a driver that has the Hazmat Endorsement on their CDL retake the state Hazmat written test?
options: Every three years when license is renewed
Every four years when license is renewed
Every five years when license is renewed
None of the answers are correct
questions.explanation: Generally, you must renew every five years, although some states may require more frequent reviews based on shorter license cycles. You will be required to submit new fingerprints at the time of renewal of the endorsement.

questions.question: Do you need to stop before a railroad crossing if you are hauling 100 pounds of Division 4.3 materials?
options: It is impossible to tell without more information.
Yes, but only if the arm is down telling vehicles to stop.
questions.explanation: Stop before a railroad crossing if your vehicle: Is placarded, carries any amount of chlorine, has cargo tanks whether loaded or empty used for hazardous materials.

questions.question: You are transporting hazardous materials. When you are not behind the wheel, the shipping papers must be on the driver's seat or
options: on the dashboard in clear view.
in the pouch on the driver's door.
questions.explanation: You must also keep shipping papers: In a pouch on the driver's door, or in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is the proper definition of a cargo tank?
options: A bulk container permanently attached to a vehicle
A bulk container not permanently attached to a vehicle
questions.explanation: Cargo tanks are bulk packaging permanently attached to a vehicle. Cargo tanks remain on the vehicle when you load and unload them.

questions.question: A truck has hazardous material, when can it be moved without the placards on the truck?
options: When the shipper says it's ok
questions.explanation: You are only allowed to move an improperly placarded vehicle during an emergency, in order to protect life or property

questions.question: The basic description of a hazardous material includes the hazard class, the id number, and the proper shipping name. Which one must appear first on the shipping paper?
questions.explanation: The basic description of hazardous materials includes the identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class or division, and the packing group, if any, in that order.

questions.question: A vehicle contains 500 pounds each of Division 1.1 explosives and Division 1.2 explosives. You must have
questions.explanation: The Placards Table 1 contains explosives, so any amount being transported needs to have placards displayed on the vehicle, with the proper division number.

questions.question: When hauling hazardous materials, you must check any dual tires
options: at the start of each trip and each time you stop.
questions.explanation: If you have a placarded trailer with dual tires, you should check the tires at the start of each trip and each time that you stop for any reason, whether to rest or to refuel. Use a tire pressure gauge to get an accurate reading.

questions.question: Which three hazard classes should not be loaded into a trailer that has a heater or air conditioner unit.
questions.explanation: Anything explosive or flammable should not be loaded into a trailer with heaters or air conditioners because of the possibility of a malfunction creating a spark that could lead to an explosion.

questions.question: The intent of hazardous materials regulations is to ensure safety, to contain the material, and:
questions.explanation: The three intents are: Contain the Material; Communicate the Risk; and Assure Safe Drivers and Equipment.

questions.question: If you are carrying Division 1.2 or 1.3 materials, how far away must you park from the traveled portion of the roadway?
questions.explanation: Never park with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within five feet of the traveled part of the road.

questions.question: Why must the shipper sign the shipping paper?
options: To certify that it has prepared the shipment in accordance with regulations
To certify that it accepts liability for an accident
To certify that the entire shipment is present and accounted for before the carrier accepts it
questions.explanation: A statement on a shipping paper, signed by the shipper, saying they prepared the shipment properly according to law.

questions.question: You find an overheated tire during an enroute inspection. If you are hauling hazardous materials, you must:
options: Wait at least 2 hours before continuing your trip
Cool the tire, then check it every 2 hours
Remove the tire and place it in the spare tire rack
Remove the tire and place it a safe distance from the vehicle
questions.explanation: Remove any overheated tire. Place it a safe distance from your vehicle. Don't drive until you correct the cause of the overheating.

questions.question: The transport index of a radioactive material:
options: Is another way of writing the weight of the package.
Tells the degree of control needed during transportation
Is something that only the shipper needs to worry about
questions.explanation: Radiation surrounds each package, passing through all nearby packages. To deal with this problem, the number of packages you can load together is controlled. Their closeness to people, animals, and unexposed film is also controlled. The transport index tells the degree of control needed during transportation.

questions.question: An "A or W" the first column of the hazardous materials table means:
options: It is ok to ship this material by air only
There are no restrictions with this material if shipped by water only
This material has no restrictions when shipped by air and/or water
This material is only restricted when shipped by air and/or water
questions.explanation: Means the hazardous material described in Column 2 is subject to the HMR only when offered or intended for transport by air and/or water unless it is a hazardous substance or hazardous waste.

questions.question: The intent of hazardous materials regulations is to ensure safety, to contain the material, and:
questions.explanation: The three intents are: Contain the Material; Communicate the Risk; and Assure Safe Drivers and Equipment.

questions.question: Which of the following must drivers have in their possession while transporting class 1.1 or 1.3 explosives?
questions.explanation: If transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, you must have a written route plan and follow that plan. Carriers prepare the route plan in advance and give the driver a copy

questions.question: There are three lists that drivers, shippers and carriers use to find out if a material is regulated as hazardous. Which one of these choices is not one of those three lists?
options: List of hazardous substances and reportable quantities
questions.explanation: There are three main lists used by shippers, carriers, and drivers when trying to identify hazardous materials. Hazardous Materials Table, List of Hazardous Substances and Reportable Quantities, List of Marine Pollutants.

tanker.name: Tanker
tanker.description: Practice tests for the Tanker endorsement

questions.question: Hauling liquids in tankers requires special care for two reasons. One reason is the _____ center of gravity that tankers have.
questions.explanation: Hauling liquids in tanks requires special skills because of the high center of gravity and liquid movement.

questions.question: You are driving a tank truck and the front wheels begin to skid. Which of these is most likely to occur?
options: You will continue in a straight line and keep moving forward no matter how much you steer
Liquid surge will pull the tank from the truck
questions.explanation: In a front-wheel skid, the front end tends to go in a straight line regardless of how much you turn the steering wheel.

questions.question: How far back does a helper stand when pumping or unloading liquids from a tanker?
questions.explanation: The person watching the loading or unloading must: be alert, have a clear view of the cargo tank, be within 25 feet of the tank, know of the hazards of the materials involved, know the procedures to follow in an emergency, and be authorized to move the cargo tank and able to do so.

questions.question: Outage means:
questions.explanation: Liquids expand as they warm and you must leave room for the expanding liquid. This is called "outage."

questions.question: Side to side surge can cause:
questions.explanation: Side-to-side surge can cause a roll over.

questions.question: You need to be extremely cautious when driving smooth bore tankers. This is especially true when you are:
options: Hauling milk or other food products
questions.explanation: Un-baffled liquid tankers (sometimes called "smooth bore" tanks) have nothing inside to slow down the flow of the liquid. Therefore, forward-and back surge is very strong.

questions.question: Liquid in a tank with baffles can have what kind of surge?
questions.explanation: The baffles help to control the forward and backward liquid surge. Side-to-side surge can still occur. This can cause a roll over.

questions.question: When your cargo tank has baffles, what handling effect do you expect?
options: There will be less side to side surge than there is in tanks without baffles
There will be less front to back surge than there is in tanks without baffles
There will be slower surge than quick surge
questions.explanation: The baffles help to control the forward and backward liquid surge. Side-to-side surge can still occur. This can cause a roll over.

questions.question: Which of these statements about stopping distance and speed is true?
options: You need about two times as much stopping distance at 40 MPH as at 20 MPH
Wet roads can double stopping distance at any speed
questions.explanation: Remember that wet roads double the normal stopping distance.

questions.question: Which of these statements about tankers and their center of gravity is true?
options: Much of the load's weight is carried high up off the road.
Tankers can turn over at the speed limits posted for curves.
questions.explanation: High center of gravity means that much of the load's weight is carried high up off the road. This makes the vehicle top-heavy and easy to roll over. Liquid tankers are especially easy to roll over. Tests have shown that tankers can turn over at the speed limits posted for curves. Take highway curves and on ramp/off ramp curves well below the posted speeds

questions.question: You must have a tank vehicle (N) endorsement to drive a vehicle with
options: individual tanks over 225 gallons or a total of at least 2,400 gallons.
individual tanks over 119 gallons or a total of at least 1,000 gallons.
individual tanks over 65 gallons or a total of at least 500 gallons.
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required if your vehicle needs a Class A or B CDL and you want to haul a liquid or liquid gas in a tank or tanks having an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1000 gallons or more that is either permanently or temporarily attached to the vehicle or the chassis.

questions.question: When should you inspect a tank vehicle?
options: Before loading it, driving it, or unloading it
Before loading it or driving it
questions.explanation: You should inspect a tank vehicle before loading it, driving it, or unloading it. This is to ensure that it is safe to carry out these activities and the vehicle can safely hold its liquid or gas contents.

questions.question: To control surge, what is the best way to brake?
options: Keep a steady foot on the brake and don't release the brake too soon.
Brake quickly to slow down and then brake quickly again to come to a full stop.
questions.explanation: Keep a steady pressure on the brakes. Do not release too soon when coming to a stop. Brake far in advance of a stop and increase your following distance.

questions.question: When must a tank be un-baffled?
options: If the liquid is likely to expand a lot
If the liquid is very dense
If it has to stay very clean
questions.explanation: Un-baffled liquid tankers sometimes called "smooth bore" tanks have nothing inside to slow down the flow of the liquid. Un-baffled tanks are usually those that transport food products like milk. Sanitation regulations forbid the use of baffles because of the difficulty in cleaning the inside of the tank.

questions.question: Which of these is the most important thing to remember about emergency braking?
options: If the wheels are skidding, you cannot control the vehicle.
Disconnecting the steering axle brakes will help keep your vehicle in a straight line.
Never do it without downshifting first.
questions.explanation: If the wheels are skidding, you cannot control the vehicle.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop, brake so that
options: you can use the parking brake before the brake pedal.
your vehicle will stay in a straight line.
questions.explanation: You should brake in a way that will keep your vehicle in a straight line and allow you to turn if it becomes necessary. You can use the "controlled braking" method or the "stab braking" method.

questions.question: If your vehicle has any of the following equipment, what needs to work properly?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has any of the following equipment, make sure it works: vapor recovery kits, grounding and bonding cables, emergency shut-off systems, or built in fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If a hill or curve keeps drivers behind you from seeing the vehicle within 500 feet:
options: the rear reflective triangle should be moved back down the road to give adequate warning
You do not need to put out reflective triangles unless the vehicle will be stopped for 30 minutes or more
The vehicles taillights should be kept on warning other drivers
questions.explanation: If line of sight view is obstructed due to hill or curve, move the rear-most triangle to a point back down the road so warning is provided up to 500 feet.

questions.question: When you load the small tanks of a cargo tank equipped with bulkheads, you should check your:
questions.explanation: Some liquid tanks are divided into several smaller tanks by bulkheads. When loading and unloading the smaller tanks, the driver must pay attention to weight distribution. Don't put too much weight on the front or rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: When you unload the smaller tanks of a tank with bulk heads, be careful to check the:
