questions.explanation: When loading and unloading the smaller tanks, the driver must pay attention to weight distribution. Don't put too much weight on the front or rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: How would you expect a truck with a cargo tank that has baffles to handle on the road?
options: The truck will seem heavier than it really is
There will be less front to back surge than there is in a tanker without baffles
The truck will handle the same as a tanker without baffles
questions.explanation: Baffled liquid tanks have bulkheads in them with holes that let the liquid flow through. The baffles help to control the forward and backward liquid surge. Side-to-side surge can still occur. This can cause a roll over.

questions.question: Separations between compartments inside tanks that have openings or holes in them are called?
questions.explanation: Baffled liquid tanks have bulkheads in them with holes that let the liquid flow through. The baffles help to control the forward and backward liquid surge.

questions.question: An emergency forces you to stop your tanker quickly or crash. You should:
options: Lock the brakes with the pedal and hold it there
questions.explanation: You should brake in a way that will keep your vehicle in a straight line and allow you to turn if it becomes necessary. You can use the "controlled braking" method or the "stab braking" method.

questions.question: The best way to take a curve with a tanker is to slow to a safe speed before entering the curve, then _____ as you go through it.
questions.explanation: Slow down before curves, then accelerate slightly through the curve. The posted speed for a curve may be too fast for a tank vehicle.

questions.question: When loading a tanker that has 3 or 4 valves at the bottom of the tanker, you should have the valves?
questions.explanation: Never drive or load a tank vehicle with open valves or manhole covers.

questions.question: Outage depends on
options: the temperatures that your vehicle will be subjected to.
questions.explanation: Since different liquids expand by different amounts, they require different amounts of outage. You must know the outage requirement when hauling liquids in bulk.

questions.question: If you steer quickly while braking, your tanker may
questions.explanation: Because of the high center of gravity and the surge of the liquid, you must start, slow down, and stop very smoothly. Also, make smooth turns and lane changes.

questions.question: You may not be able to fill the tanks completely because
options: the liquid may expand in transit.
a full load of a dense liquid may exceed the legal weight limit.
both of the above are true.
questions.explanation: A full tank of dense liquid (such as some acids) may exceed legal weight limits. For that reason, you may often only partially fill tanks with heavy liquids. The amount of liquid to load into a tank depends on: the amount the liquid will expand in transit, the weight of the liquid, and the legal weight limits.

questions.question: What should you do if you get stuck on the railroad tracks?
options: Get out of your vehicle and away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If for any reason you get stuck on the tracks, get out of the vehicle and away from the tracks. Check signposts or signal housing at the crossing for emergency notification information. Call 911 or another emergency number. Give the location of the crossing using all identifiable landmarks, especially the DOT number, if posted.

questions.question: A vehicle placarded for hazardous materials must have placards on ____ sides.
questions.explanation: You placard your vehicle to warn everyone around you that you are transporting hazardous materials. Therefore, you must have placards on all four sides of your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you start moving without rolling backward?
options: Engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake.
Apply the trailer brake hand valve.
Set the parking brake whenever necessary.
questions.explanation: Don't roll back when you start. You may hit someone behind you. If you have a manual transmission vehicle, partly engage the clutch before you take your right foot off the brake. Put on the parking brake whenever necessary to keep from rolling back. Release the parking brake only when you have applied enough engine power to keep from rolling back.

questions.question: You should know the outage needed for the liquids you carry because?
options: Some of the heaviest liquids do not need any
Tank baffles are not always legal with outage
Some liquids expand more than others when they get warm
questions.explanation: Liquids expand as they warm and you must leave room for the expanding liquid. This is called "outage." Since different liquids expand by different amounts, they require different amounts of outage.

questions.question: You are driving on a clear night, you must dim your headlights from high to low, and should adjust your speed so you can stop within:
options: The distance you will travel in the next 15 seconds
The distance you can see ahead
The length of a football field
questions.explanation: You should always be able to stop within the distance you can see ahead. Fog, rain, or other conditions may require that you slowdown to be able to stop in the distance you can see. At night, you can't see as far with low beams as you can with high beams. When you must use low beams, slow down.

questions.question: Empty trucks:
options: Stop quicker when you use only the emergency or parking brake
Have better traction when stopping than full ones
May require longer stopping distances than full ones
questions.explanation: Empty tank vehicles may take longer to stop than full ones.

questions.question: Baffles in liquid cargo tanks do not usually prevent the movement of surge from:
questions.explanation: Baffles slow front to back surge in tankers but have little effect on side to side surge.

questions.question: Liquid tight separations between compartments inside tanks are called:
questions.explanation: Some liquid tanks are divided into several smaller tanks by bulkheads.

questions.question: The movement of the liquid in partially filled tanks is called
questions.explanation: Liquid surge results from movement of the liquid in partially filled tanks. This movement can have bad effects on handling. When the wave hits the end or sides of the tank, it tends to push the truck in the direction the wave is moving.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is required for certain vehicles that transport
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required for certain vehicles that transport liquids or gases. The liquid or gas does not have to be a hazardous material.

questions.question: When loading a tank with bulkheads, don't put too much weight on ________ of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Don't put too much weight on the front or rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: On a long or steep downgrade, once you have reached your "safe" speed, brake until you are traveling
questions.explanation: The use of brakes on a long and/or steep downgrade is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine. Once the vehicle is in the proper low gear, the following are the proper braking techniques: apply the brakes just hard enough to feel a definite slowdown, when your speed has been reduced to approximately five mph below your "safe" speed then release the brakes, when your speed has increased to your "safe" speed, repeat.

questions.question: Manhole covers should be
options: left partially open to prevent a buildup of fumes.
opened and reclosed before you drive the vehicle.
closed before you drive the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Never drive a tank vehicle with open valves or manhole covers.

questions.question: If you do not have an automatic tank drain, when should you drain your air tanks?
options: After every four hours of service
At the end of each working day
questions.explanation: If your vehicle does not have automatic air tank drains, drain your air tanks at the end of each working day to remove moisture and oil. Otherwise, the brakes could fail.

questions.question: Exactly how should you inspect your tank vehicle?
options: Do it the same way that you inspected other tank vehicles before.
Read the vehicle's manual to learn how to do it.
Ask a fellow driver how to do it.
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have special items that you need to check. Tank vehicles come in many types and sizes. You need to check the vehicle's operator manual to make sure you know how to inspect your tank vehicle.

questions.question: A smooth bore tank is also known as
questions.explanation: Un-baffled liquid tankers also called smooth bore" tanks have nothing inside to slow down the flow of the liquid.

questions.question: Liquid surge is especially dangerous
questions.explanation: If the truck is on a slippery surface such as ice, the wave can shove a stopped truck out into an intersection.

questions.question: Which of these statements about emergency steering and tankers is true?
options: A tanker is easier to counter steer than most vehicles
When making a quick steering movement, do not apply the brakes
You should wrap your thumbs around the steering wheel before starting a quick steering movement
questions.explanation: If you must make a quick steering movement, applying the brakes would cause liquid surge increasing the chance of a roll over.

questions.question: You should be extremely cautious when driving smooth bore tankers, especially when you are:
options: Going up or down a hill
questions.explanation: Be extremely cautious in driving smooth bore tanks, especially when starting and stopping.

questions.question: If you drive a tank vehicle that you know is leaking, you may
options: receive a citation and be prevented from further driving.
questions.explanation: Don't carry liquids or gases in a leaking tank. To do so is a crime. You will be cited and prevented from driving further. You may also be liable for the clean-up of any spill.

questions.question: If your vehicle is placarded, you must stop _______ feet before the nearest rail at a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Stop before a railroad crossing if your vehicle: Is placarded, carries any amount of chlorine, has cargo tanks loaded or empty used for hazardous materials. You must stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail. Proceed only when you are sure no train is coming, and you can clear the tracks without stopping. Don't shift gears while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: To correct a drive-wheel braking skid, you should
options: brake harder, turn quickly, and counter-steer.
stop braking, turn quickly, and counter-steer.
questions.explanation: Do the following to correct a drive-wheel braking skid: stop braking allowing the rear wheels roll again and keep the rear wheels from sliding, and counter-steer. As a vehicle turns back on course, it tends to keep on turning, unless you turn the steering wheel quickly the other way, you may find yourself skidding in the opposite direction.

questions.question: When pre-tripping your tanker you should check for?
questions.explanation: On all tank vehicles, the most important item to check for is leaks. Check under and around the vehicle for signs of any leaking. Don't carry liquids or gases in a leaking tank.

questions.question: What does liquid surge do to the handling of a tanker?
options: Surge raises the wind drag of the truck
Surge can move the truck in the direction the liquid waves move
Surge lets you turn corners tighter
questions.explanation: Liquid surge results from movement of the liquid in partially filled tanks. This movement can have bad effects on handling. When the wave hits the end of the tank, it tends to push the truck in the direction the wave is moving.

questions.question: When hauling 2 tankers, where should the weight be carried?
questions.explanation: For the safest handling on the road, the more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in first position behind the tractor. The lighter trailer should be in the rear.

questions.question: You should know that your brakes are fading when:
options: You must push harder on the brake pedal to control your speed on a downgrade.
The brake feels spongy when pressure is applied.
Pressure on the brake pedal is released and speed increases.
questions.explanation: Increasing application pressure to hold the same speed means the brakes are fading.

questions.question: The amount of liquid to load into a tank depends on:
options: The amount the liquid will expand in transit
questions.explanation: The amount of liquid to load into a tank depends on: the amount the liquid will expand in transit, the weight of the liquid, and legal weight limits.

questions.question: Which of these statements about managing space to the sides is true?
options: Strong winds make it easy to stay in your lane.
You should avoid traveling next to others whenever possible.
Always keep your vehicle to the right side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles are often wide and take up most of a lane. Safe drivers will manage what little space they have. You can do this by keeping your vehicle centered in your lane and avoid driving alongside others.

questions.question: Hauling liquids in tank vehicles requires special care for two reasons. One reason is:
questions.explanation: Hauling liquids in tanks requires special skills because of the high center of gravity and liquid movement.

questions.question: Loaded tankers are said to have a high center of gravity. What does this mean?
options: Much of the tanker's weight is low, toward the ground.
Much of the tanker's weight is high up off the ground.
The top of the tanker is far away from the Earth's gravity.
questions.explanation: High center of gravity means that much of the load's weight is carried high up off the road. This makes the vehicle top-heavy and easy to roll over. Tests have shown that tankers can turn over at the speed limits posted for curves.

questions.question: A tanker has lost its brakes. When should the driver use a truck escape ramp?
options: Only if the tank has baffles
questions.explanation: Any driver who loses brakes going downhill should use an escape ramp if it's available. If you don't use it, your chances of having a serious crash may be much greater.

questions.question: When hauling hazardous materials, you must check any dual tires
options: at the start of each trip and each time you stop.
questions.explanation: If you have a placarded trailer with dual tires, you should check the tires at the start of each trip and each time that you stop for any reason, whether to rest or to refuel. Use a tire pressure gauge to get an accurate reading.

school-bus.name: School Bus
school-bus.description: Practice tests for the School Bus endorsement

questions.question: What do the red flashing lights on an eight-light system bus signify to other drivers?
options: The school bus is stopped for a red light
The school bus is stopped for a train crossing
The school bus is stopped because it is broken down
The school bus is stopped to pick up or discharge pupils
questions.explanation: Red flashing lights on a school bus indicate that the bus is stopped to pick up or discharge students.

questions.question: While looking through the interior flat mirror the driver should have a clear view of?
questions.explanation: The large flat mirror hanging above the driver's head is there for them to see all of the students onboard at one time.

questions.question: How far prior to a bus pick up location must the amber warning lights be turned on?
questions.explanation: If the school bus is so equipped, activate alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop or in accordance with state law.

questions.question: If an unruly student is threatening the safety of others how should you handle the situation?
options: Move student to set closer to you
Remove student from the bus immediately
Pull bus to the side of the road and firmly explain the rules and regulations to the unruly student
questions.explanation: Tips on handling serious problems: stop the bus parking in a safe location off the road perhaps a parking lot or a driveway, secure the bus, take the ignition key with you if you leave your seat, stand up and speak respectfully to the offender or offenders. Speak in a courteous manner with a firm voice. Remind the offender of the expected behavior. Do not show anger but do show that you mean business.

questions.question: The school buses stop arm is to only be operated with the:
options: Yellow warning and red warning lights
Whenever the driver wants to stop traffic
questions.explanation: Activate alternating red lights when traffic is a safe distance from the school bus and ensure stop arm is extended.

questions.question: If a bus is being operated on a divided highway or a highway with four lanes or more which of the following describes the procedures for pick up and discharge of students?
options: The students can only be picked up or dropped off on the resident side of the road
The students can be dropped off or picked up on either side of the highway
The students must be picked up and dropped off in the center of the road
questions.explanation: Students could only be picked up from the resident side of the road, meaning the right side, they will not allow students to cross a major highway to get to the bus.

questions.question: When leaving a freeway, you should begin to slow down?
questions.explanation: You should start to slow down at least 100 feet in advance.

questions.question: When is it required to stop a bus, look, listen, open the driver's side window and service door?
options: Whenever the bus is stopped to pick up students
Whenever the bus is stopped to discharge students
Whenever it is extremely hot outside
Whenever the bus is stopped at a railroad crossing
questions.explanation: At the Crossing: Stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, place the transmission in Park. turn off all radios and noisy equipment, silence the passengers, and open the service door and driver's window. Look and listen for an approaching train.

questions.question: In flat mirrors you should see?
options: Full side of the bus and rear of bus
Pedestrians on the side walk on both sides of the bus
questions.explanation: Ensure that the flat mirrors are properly adjusted so you can see: 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus, along the sides of the bus, and the rear tires touching the ground.

questions.question: During your pre-trip vehicle inspection test, make sure that
options: the emergency exits are undamaged, operate smoothly, and close securely from the inside.
the emergency exit warning devices (if so equipped) are working.
both of the above are true.
questions.explanation: Make sure that all emergency exits are not damaged, operate smoothly, and close securely from the inside. Check that any emergency exit warning devices are working.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about students who must cross in front of the bus after exiting it?
options: The driver should make a U-turn, so those students won't have to cross in front of the bus after exiting it.
When the driver signals that it is safe to proceed, the students should cross the street while remaining in the driver's view.
When the driver signals that it is safe to proceed, the students should run across the street to reduce their exposure to danger.
questions.explanation: Wait for your signal before crossing the roadway. Upon your signal, the students should: Cross far enough in front of the school bus to be in your view.

questions.question: A passive railroad crossing
options: doesn't have any type of traffic control device.
is a railroad crossing at which you don't have to stop.
questions.explanation: This type of crossing does not have any type of traffic control device. You must stop at these crossings and follow proper procedures. However, the decision to proceed rests entirely in your hands.

questions.question: As part of your vehicle inspection test, you will have to check _________ to be sure that it is undamaged, operating smoothly, and able to be closed securely from the inside.
questions.explanation: As part of your vehicle inspection test, you will have to check one emergency exit to be sure that it is undamaged, operating smoothly, and able to be closed securely from the inside. You will also have to point out the other emergency exits and describe how they operate.

questions.question: Properly adjusted, the outside left and right side convex mirrors will let you see
options: at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus.
the front of the rear tires touching the ground.
questions.explanation: You should position these mirrors to see: the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, the front of the rear tires touching the ground, and at least one traffic lane on either side of the bus.

questions.question: You can change the location of a school bus stop
options: if there is a better location nearby.
only with the written approval of the school district.
only if all the passengers agree to the change.
questions.explanation: You should never change the location of a bus stop without written approval from the appropriate school district official.

questions.question: When you inspect the battery and battery box during your pre-trip vehicle inspection test, make sure that
options: the battery is secure, connections are tight with minimal corrosion, and cell caps are present.
the battery box and cover or door are secure.
both of the above are true.
questions.explanation: Wherever located, see that battery(s) are secure, connections are tight, and cell caps are present. Battery connections should not show signs of excessive corrosion.

questions.question: The left and right danger zones extend up to _______ from the left and right sides of the school bus.
questions.explanation: The danger zones may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous, 10 feet from the left and right sides of the bus and 10 feet behind the rear bumper of the school bus.

questions.question: When driving a school bus in high winds, you should
options: tailgate a big truck so it can shield you from the wind.
speed up to get away from the wind as quickly as possible.
keep a strong grip on the steering wheel and try to anticipate gusts.
questions.explanation: Strong winds affect the handling of the school bus! The side of a school bus acts like a sail on a sailboat. Strong winds can push the school bus sideways. They can even move the school bus off the road or, in extreme conditions, tip it over.

questions.question: The convex, crossover, and flat mirrors should be viewed
options: in a logical sequence to ensure that a child or object is not in any of the danger zones.
every 10 seconds and more often in heavy traffic.
questions.explanation: All mirrors should be viewed in a logical sequence to ensure that a child or object is not in any of the danger zones.

questions.question: What is the "golden rule" for school buses when approaching and crossing railroad tracks?
options: Stop, look, and turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: At the Crossing: stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, place the transmission in Park, turn off all radios and noisy equipment, silence the passengers, open the service door and driver's window, and look and listen for an approaching train.

questions.question: Which of the following people can remove or suspend a student from riding the bus?
options: The school principal, superintendent, or the superintendent's designee
questions.explanation: Follow your school's procedures for discipline or refusal of rights to ride the bus. If you feel that the offense is serious enough that you cannot safely drive the bus, call for a school administrator or the police to come and remove the student.

questions.question: What would be considered proper procedure at a highway railroad crossing?
options: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad
questions.explanation: When approaching turn on the hazard lights, and do not shift when crossing the tracks.

questions.question: When getting onto a highway you should?
options: Keep your eyes on the car in front of you and watch mirrors for gaps
questions.explanation: When entering a highway, you should make sure there are no sudden changes by the car in front of you, while checking the mirrors for the proper gap to merge.

questions.question: When is the use of alcohol, tobacco, and non-prescription drugs allowed on the school bus?
options: Only when the bus driver says it is ok
questions.explanation: The use of alcohol, tobacco, and non-prescription drugs should not be allowed on the school bus.

questions.question: What do Anti-Lock Brakes do?
options: Apply more breaking force to the front axle
Help the breaks lock when they refuse to
Prevent breaks from locking up when hard pressure is applied
questions.explanation: ABS is a computerized system that keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications.

questions.question: While the bus is running when is the driver allowed to exit the bus?
questions.explanation: If the vehicle is running the driver is not allowed to leave the vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about evacuation procedures is true?
options: If time allows, notify the dispatch office about your situation, your location, and the type of assistance you need.
If time allows, back up to a safe location before evacuating the bus.
If time allows, walk through the bus and close all the windows.
questions.explanation: If time allows, notify dispatch office of evacuation location, conditions, and type of assistance needed.

questions.question: When unloading students at a school, you should
options: stand outside the bus in front of a crossover mirror to supervise unloading.
leave the engine running so you can drive away when the students have exited.
tell the students to remain seated until they are told to exit.
questions.explanation: Have the students remain seated until told to exit.

questions.question: The blind spot behind the bus may extend up to ________, depending on the length and width of the bus.
questions.explanation: The blind spot behind the bus extends 5o to 150 feet and could extend up to 400 feet depending on the length and width of the bus.

questions.question: When can you put a misbehaving student off the bus?
options: If the behavior is serious enough
Only at school or the student's designated bus stop
questions.explanation: Never put a student off the bus except at school or at his or her designated school bus stop. If you feel that the offense is serious enough that you cannot safely drive the bus, call for a school administrator or the police to come and remove the student.

questions.question: Before leaving, make sure the students are in plain view
options: at least 10 to 15 feet away from the side of the bus.
at least 25 feet away from the side of the bus.
questions.explanation: Tell students to exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students.

questions.question: You have stopped your bus to load students. Before you signal them to approach the bus, you should
options: turn on the alternating flashing red lights.
questions.explanation: Monitor all mirrors continuously.

questions.question: Why is it so critical for you to understand the loading and unloading procedures?
options: Because drivers tend to ignore students walking to school
Because only high school students understand how to cross the road
Because so many students are killed each year while getting on or off school buses
questions.explanation: More students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside of a school bus. As a result, knowing what to do before, during, and after loading or unloading students is critical.

questions.question: In an emergency, you should consider NOT evacuating students from your school bus
options: if their injuries might be worsened by moving them.
if they would be exposed to downed power lines or other hazards.
in either of the above situations.
questions.explanation: A decision to evacuate should include consideration of the following conditions: fire or danger of fire; smell of raw or leaking fuel; the chance the bus could be hit by other vehicles; downed power lines; exposing students to speeding traffic, severe weather, or a dangerous environment; when moving a student complicate injury; or a hazardous spill.

questions.question: To load students after you have stopped the school bus,
options: put the transmission in park or neutral and set the parking brake.
count the number of students at the bus stop and make sure that all of them board the bus.
load students two abreast when possible for efficiency.
questions.explanation: Count the number of students at the bus stop and be sure all board the bus. If possible, know names of students at each stop. If there is a student missing, ask the other students where the student is.

questions.question: Which school bus accidents should be reported?
options: Only those involving injury or death
questions.explanation: All school bus accidents must be reported whether or not they involve death, injury, or property damage.

questions.question: Who is responsible for handling discipline problems on your school bus?
questions.explanation: Tips on handling serious problems: follow your school's procedures for discipline or refusal of rights to ride the bus, stop and park in a safe location off the road, secure the bus taking the ignition key with you if you leave your seat.

questions.question: An active railroad crossing is
options: a railroad crossing that has a traffic control device.
a railroad crossing without traffic control devices.
a railroad crossing at which you don't have to stop.
questions.explanation: This type of crossing has a traffic control device installed at the crossing to regulate traffic at the crossing. These active devices include flashing red lights, with or without bells and flashing red lights with bells and gates.

questions.question: The tail swing of a school bus can be as much as
questions.explanation: A school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing. You need to check your mirrors before and during any turning movements to monitor the tail swing.

questions.question: In addition to spare electrical fuses (if equipped), three red reflective triangles, and a working fire extinguisher, emergency equipment for a school bus includes
options: a first-aid kit and a body fluid cleanup kit.
three flares and a bolt cutter.
questions.explanation: In addition to checking for spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles, and a properly charged and rated fire extinguisher, school bus drivers must also inspect the following emergency equipment: Emergency Kit Body, and Fluid Cleanup Kit

questions.question: How could one distinguish a blind person among other pedestrians?
options: Will be walking a black dog
Will be carrying a white cane
They will only be at designated crossing areas
questions.explanation: A white cane is typically used by the blind to help them find their way around without tripping.

questions.question: When, according to the pupil transportation operation and safety rules, are the four-way hazard lights supposed to be used?
options: When stopped or parked along a road due to a breakdown
When backing up or turning around
questions.explanation: Four-way flashers or hazard lights are to be used at railroad crossings, when parked along the road from a breakdown, and whenever you are backing up or turning around.

questions.question: When is the only time the red warning lights can be used?
options: Whenever the bus is picking up or discharging students
questions.explanation: The red flashing lights are for picking up and discharging as student only.

questions.question: Front tire tread depth should be at least?
questions.explanation: Front axle or steer axel tires must have a tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch.

questions.question: What color are all school buses painted?
questions.explanation: The National Highway Transportation Safety Administration issued guidelines to the states on pupil transportation safety. One of these guidelines is that all school buses should be painted National School Bus Glossy Yellow.

questions.question: When several students are exiting the bus, the driver should count the students, if one is missing?
options: The driver should check all mirrors again
Ask the other students if they have seen the missing student
Get off the bus and locate the student
questions.explanation: Count the number of students while unloading to confirm the location of all students before pulling away from the stop. If you cannot account for a student outside the bus, secure the bus, and check around and underneath the bus.

questions.question: Before you proceed through a railroad crossing, make sure that your bus will have enough containment to completely clear the railroad tracks. As a general rule, adequate containment is
options: the length of the bus plus 15 feet.
the length of the bus plus 10 feet.
the length of the bus plus 25 feet.
questions.explanation: As a general rule, add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area.

questions.question: What is the most important reason for performing a school bus inspection?
options: To give the mechanics something to do
For safety as required by federal, state, and local laws
questions.explanation: The purpose of school bus inspections is to ensure safety. A vehicle defect found during an inspection could save you problems later. Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles.

questions.question: During your post-trip inspection of your school bus, you should check
questions.explanation: During your post-trip inspection, you should check all the mechanical and operational systems of the school bus for any problems. Immediately report any problems to your supervisor or school authorities.

questions.question: In most states, school buses are equipped with ________ warning light system to control traffic at school bus stops.
questions.explanation: Federal regulations require school buses to be equipped with a warning light system. Each bus must have two flashing red lights in front and two in the rear, and optionally two flashing amber lights in front and two in the rear.

questions.question: The front danger zone extends up to ________ from the front bumper of the school bus.
questions.explanation: The danger zones may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous, 10 feet from the left and right sides of the bus and 10 feet behind the rear bumper of the school bus.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, you should
options: activate your alternating flashing amber lights.
questions.explanation: When approaching the stop, you should: approach cautiously at a slow rate of speed; look for pedestrians, traffic, or other objects before, during, and after coming to a stop; continuously check all mirrors; activate alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop or in accordance with state law.

questions.question: Is the bus driver allowed to pick up or discharge students at other than their assigned locations?
options: Only if the school district allows and a written note from a parent has been received
Only if the bus driver wants to
Only one time a month can this be done
questions.explanation: If the school district allows this, and there is a written note from the parent, then yes, the driver can discharge at another location.

questions.question: Who is the person responsible for the daily pre-trip bus inspections?
options: The schools bus mechanic and the bus driver
The schools designated pre-trip inspection person
questions.explanation: The bus driver is responsible for preforming the pre-trip inspection daily.

questions.question: Students may never walk within how many feet of the bus at any time?
questions.explanation: The danger zone is the area on all sides of the bus where children are in the most danger of being hit, either by another vehicle or their own bus. The danger zones may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous, 10 feet from the left and right sides of the bus and 10 feet behind the rear bumper of the school bus.

questions.question: After you decide on the best type of evacuation, what must you do next?
options: Notify the dispatch office of the evacuation.
Dangle the radio telephone or microphone out of the driver's window for later use.
questions.explanation: Secure the bus by: Placing transmission in Park, setting parking brakes, shut off the engine, remove ignition key, and activate hazard-warning lights.

questions.question: Most states require school bus drivers to take a physical examination
questions.explanation: Most states require school bus drivers to have an annual physical (including a vision test) to confirm that they are still fit to perform the duties of a school bus driver.

questions.question: Which mirrors let you view the front danger zone?
questions.explanation: Crossover Mirrors are mounted on both left and right front corners of the bus. They are used to see the front bumper "danger zone" area directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision.

questions.question: During your vehicle inspection test, you must check that the entry door is undamaged. Also check that it
options: operates smoothly and closes securely from the inside.
operates smoothly and closes securely from the outside.
operates smoothly and closes securely by remote control.
questions.explanation: Check that the entry door is not damaged, operates smoothly, and closes securely from the inside.

questions.question: During your vehicle inspection test, if your school bus is equipped with a handicap lift, you should check
options: that no parts are missing, leaking, or damaged and the lift is at least 50% retracted.
that no parts are missing, leaking, or damaged and the lift is fully retracted and latched.
that the lift goes up and down smoothly.
questions.explanation: If equipped with a handicap lift, look for leaking, damaged, or missing parts and explain how lift should be checked for correct operation. Lift must be fully retracted and latched securely.

questions.question: When under the age of 21 years old a driver will be considered intoxicated at?
options: More than .02 but less than .10 BAC
questions.explanation: There is a zero-tolerance policy for having alcohol in your system as the driver of a school bus.

questions.question: The right front mirror should be adjusted to see?
options: The right front tire meeting the ground
questions.explanation: Ensure that the mirrors are properly adjusted so you can see: The entire area in front of the bus from the front bumper at ground level to a point where direct vision is possible, direct vision and mirror view vision should overlap, the right and left front tires touching the ground, and the area from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: You MUST evacuate everyone from your school bus if
options: the bus is stalled on a railroad track but there is no train in sight.
the antilock brake (ABS) warning light is on.
the bus is stalled on the shoulder of a divided highway and it is getting hot inside.
questions.explanation: The driver must evacuate the bus when: the bus is on fire or there is a threat of a fire, the bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad highway crossing, the position of the bus may change and increase the danger, there is an imminent danger of collision, and there is a need to quickly evacuate because of a hazardous materials spill.

questions.question: Immediately after stopping, you should first
options: activate the alternating flashing amber lights.
activate the alternating flashing red lights and ensure that the stop arm is extended.
load the students as quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Activate alternating red lights when traffic is a safe distance from the school bus and ensure stop arm is extended.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing signal is malfunctioning, you should
options: call your dispatcher and ask for instructions.
turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: If there is no police officer, and you believe the signal is malfunctioning, call your dispatcher to report the situation and ask for instructions on how to proceed.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, you must stop
options: between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail.
between 10 and 40 feet from the nearest rail.
between 15 and 30 feet from the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: Stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where you have the best view of the tracks.

questions.question: You're about to unload students at a bus stop. Tell them that once they've exited the bus, they should
options: cross in front of the school bus.
walk 10 to 15 feet from the side of the school bus.
questions.explanation: Tell students to exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students.

questions.question: When loading or unloading students, you should check your mirrors
options: after all students have entered or exited the bus.
questions.explanation: Monitor all mirrors continuously.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing you should turn on the hazards?
options: At least 100 feet from the railroad crossing
At least 200 feet from the railroad crossing
At least 300 feet from the railroad crossing
questions.explanation: Activate hazard lights approximately 200 feet before the crossing. Make sure your intentions are known.

questions.question: When is the most dangerous time during a bus ride?
questions.explanation: When loading or unloading students they can be three times more likely to be injured.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the special dangers of loading and unloading is true?
options: Tell students to leave any dropped objects, move out of the danger zones, and get your attention to retrieve the objects.
Tell students that they can pick up any dropped objects that are not under the bus.
Tell students not to use the handrail when exiting the bus because they could get caught.
questions.explanation: Students should be told to leave any dropped object and move to a point of safety out of the danger zones and attempt to get the driver's attention to retrieve the object.

questions.question: When approaching a bus stop on a multilane roadway, you should maintain your position _________ of the rightmost lane.
questions.explanation: Move as far as possible to the right on the traveled portion of the roadway.

questions.question: While you're loading students, if you cannot account for a student, what should you do?
options: Ask other students if they saw this student.
Secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus for the student.
Look in your mirrors for the student.
questions.explanation: If you cannot account for a student outside, secure the bus, take the key, and check around and underneath the bus.

questions.question: How can a driver determine if a bus is equipped with Anti-Lock Brakes?
options: All buses equipped with ABS systems have a tag on the sun visor
When the key is turned on an ABS. light will come on and off
The bus will stop much slower
questions.explanation: Your school bus will have a yellow ABS malfunction lamp on the instrument panel if it is equipped with ABS.

questions.question: If the bus is on fire, you must
options: keep the students on the bus until first responders arrive.
evacuate the students downwind of the bus.
evacuate the students upwind of the bus.
questions.explanation: Lead students upwind of the bus if fire is present.

questions.question: Is the bus driver allowed to crack or open the service door prior to stopping to pick up a pupil?
questions.explanation: The door needs to remain shut until the bus has come to a complete stop to pick up or drop off a student.

questions.question: You should activate your alternating flashing amber warning lights ________, depending on the laws and regulations of your state.
options: 20 to 50 feet before the school bus stop
300 to 500 feet before the school bus stop
100 to 300 feet before the school bus stop
questions.explanation: If the school bus is so equipped, activate alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop or in accordance with state law.

questions.question: As part of your post-trip inspection of your bus, check for each of the following EXCEPT
options: personal belongings that were left on the bus.
dirt or shoeprints on the floor.
questions.explanation: Make sure that all emergency exits are not damaged, operate smoothly, and close securely from the inside.

questions.question: In an emergency, you MUST evacuate everyone from your school bus
options: if the position of the bus may change and further increase the danger.
if the bus is on fire.
in either of the above situations.
questions.explanation: The driver must evacuate the bus when: the bus is on fire or there is a threat of a fire, the bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad highway crossing, the position of the bus may change and increase the danger, there is an imminent danger of collision, or there is a need to quickly evacuate because of a hazardous materials spill.

questions.question: When turning around at a railroad crossing a driver should?
questions.explanation: Hazard lights would be required for both the turnaround, and the railroad crossing.

pretrip.name: Pretrip
pretrip.description: Practice tests for the Pretrip endorsement

questions.question: When doing the pre-trip, you should tell the examiner each item you are checking and 2-3 things you check each item for.
questions.explanation: Try not to overdo the item or what you are checking it for. You only get 30 minutes to check everything on the vehicle.

questions.question: Should you do an overview of your vehicle as you approach it (including looking for leaks, leaning, or excessive damage)?
questions.explanation: Overviews give you a chance to catch major problems early.

questions.question: When checking the lights at the front of the vehicle what should you check for?
options: B. That the lens covers are there, lights are securely attached, clean, and working.
C. Nothing, you do not have to check the lights.
questions.explanation: All lights will need checked at the front, back and sides of the vehicle. They will need checked for covers, cleanliness, secureness, and that they work.

questions.question: When checking the windshield, what should you be looking for?
options: A. That the windshield is there, not cracked or chipped.
B. That the windshield is there, not cracked or chipped, clean, the seals are in good condition, and not leaking.
C. That it is clean, and not leaking.
questions.explanation: Mentioning the windshield and checking it for cracks, chips, and cleanliness is not enough. You will have to check the seals and for leaks to get it marked as checked.

questions.question: When opening the hood, you should check?
options: A. The hinges, catches, and springs.
B. The important stuff is under the hood, so nothing.
questions.explanation: The hood will always need checked, mainly for damage, but don't forget the hinges, catches, and springs or you might not get credit.

questions.question: Checking the mirrors on the outside of the vehicle you should check for?
questions.explanation: Don't forget you can have mirrors on the hood, and on the doors of the cab. While outside check for mounts, cracks, and cleanliness. You should also check them again when inside the vehicle to make sure they are properly adjusted.

questions.question: In the engine compartment there are four fluids you must check, they are?
options: A. Windshield wiper fluid, oil, coolant, and moisture or leaks.
B. Transmission fluid, oil, coolant, and power steering fluid.
C. Moisture or leaks, oil, coolant, power steering fluid.
questions.explanation: It is best to check all your fluids during a pre-trip inspection, but the fluids you have to say are oil, coolant, power steering, and checking for moisture and leaks.

questions.question: In the engine compartment there are four major belt or gear driven components. What are they?
options: A. Power steering pump, fuel pump, alternator, water pump.
B. Power steering pump, fuel pump, alternator, air compressor.
C. Fuel pump, alternator, air compressor, water pump.
D. Power steering pump, alternator, air compressor, and water pump.
questions.explanation: It is best to check all your belt and gear driven components, but the power steering, alternator, air compressor, and water pump are all that appear on the CDL pre-trip.

questions.question: What should you check each of the fluids in the engine compartment for?
questions.explanation: All fluids should be at the proper level, clean, free of debris, with no leaks. You can also add proper color to this list. Some coolants are red, green and orange. Red or clear for most power steering. Oil can be difficult, it should be tan in color, but normally after use of the vehicle it gets black.

questions.question: What are the main components of the steering controls found in the engine compartment?
options: A. Upper steering linkage, gearbox, tie rod ends, and tie rod.
B. Upper steering linkage, universal joints, tie rod ends, tie rod.
C. Upper steering linkage, universal joints, power steering pump, pitman arm, drag link, tie rod ends, tie rod.
D. Upper steering linkage, universal joints, pitman arm, tie rod ends, tie rod.
questions.explanation: The steering linkage consists of upper steering linkage, universal joints, power steering pump, pitman arm, drag link, tie rod ends, tie rod. They will all need checked separately.

questions.question: What should you check the steering linkage for?
options: A. All castle nuts are tight and secure.
questions.explanation: Along with the castle nuts, cotter pins, and excessive play you can check for illegal welds and cracks.

questions.question: Which of the following does not get checked in the engine compartment?
questions.explanation: Oil pressure is checked on the inside of the cab using the oil pressure gauge.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an engine compartment belt?
questions.explanation: The safety belt secures the driver in the cab.

questions.question: The leaf springs, shocks, U-bolts, shackles, and air bags are part of what system?
questions.explanation: These are all components of the suspension system and will need checked independently in your pre-trip exam.

questions.question: Hoses in the engine compartment should be checked for?
questions.explanation: Make sure the lines are connected and secure, no frays, cracks, tears, and no leaks to get hoses marked off. The trick is you need to say horses for the air compressor, power steering, water pump independently to get credit.

questions.question: The engine belts should be checked for?
questions.explanation: Check each belt individually. There can be belts for a few different components under the hood. The excessive play of more than 3/4 of an inch.

questions.question: Brake lines should be checked for?
options: B. No frays, cracks, or damage.
questions.explanation: As with all hoses, make sure the connections are tight and secure. That there are no frays, cracks, or damage to the lines with no leaks. With an airline leaks can be found by suspicious clean spots on the hose.

questions.question: Air chambers are?
options: A. Part of the braking system.
B. Where air is stored for use.
C. Not on a commercial vehicle.
questions.explanation: Also called brake chambers, they are found on most commercial vehicles, and filled with air to apply the brakes.

questions.question: Air chambers should be checked for?
questions.explanation: Also called brake chambers, they need to be mounted tight and secure, not excessively damaged, and not leaking.

questions.question: The slack adjuster is part of the braking system, what is the maximum play allowed with the brakes off?
questions.explanation: There should be no more than 1 inch of play in any slack adjuster on the vehicle, with the brakes off.

questions.question: Brake pads should be checked for?
options: A. At least a 1/4 of an inch of life left.
questions.explanation: All answers are true. They should have at least a 1/4 inch of life left on the brake pad, since they can wear unevenly also check that they are not dangerously thin, and no cracks or breaks.

questions.question: Brake drums?
options: A. Are not out of round and have no illegal welds.
B. No cracks, or illegal welds.
C. Not out of round, no illegal welds, and no cracks.
questions.explanation: Make sure they are not misshapen (out of round), no illegal welds, and no cracks.

questions.question: Brake drums (or discs) must not have cracks longer than:
options: A. 1/2 the width of the friction area.
B. One inch across in a straight line.
questions.explanation: The area where the brake shoes touch the drum is considered the friction area, there should be no cracks 1/2 the width of that area.

questions.question: Tire tread depth depends on the axel. The depth should be no less than ______ for the steer axel, and _____ for any other axel.
questions.explanation: All tread depth needs to be said in thirty-seconds. The front axle or steer axel must have at least 4/32, and the rest of the axles can have no less than 2/32.

questions.question: Retreaded tires can be on any axel.
questions.explanation: The front or steer axel is not allowed to have retreaded tires.

questions.question: Tires should be checked for?
options: B. Cuts, cracks, bulges, and depth.
C. Cuts, cracks, bulges, and inflation.
D. Cuts, cracks, bulges, depth, and inflation.
questions.explanation: Tires should not have any cuts, cracks, or bulges. You will need to make sure the tire pressure is up to manufacturer specifications, and that it has the proper tread depth.

questions.question: You should check rims for dents, cracks, illegal welds, valve stem, and that they are tight and secure.
questions.explanation: Rims should not have dents, cracks, illegal welds. This is a great time to mention your valve stem since it comes through the rim, and the rims need to be tight and secure.

questions.question: All rims have a spacer.
questions.explanation: The front axle does not have a spacer because it does not have dual tires on each side. Also bud rims are made so that there is no need for a spacer. Only on Dayton setups would you have a spacer.

questions.question: Lug nuts (that hold the rim to the axle) should be checked for?
options: B. No worn or stripped threads.
C. No rust marks (from the lug nuts to the outside of rim).
questions.explanation: Lug nuts need to be tight and secure, no stripped or worn threads. The rust marks will start at the best of the lug nut and run to the outside of the rim and indicate a loose lug nut.

questions.question: The hub oil seal should be?
options: A. Filled to the proper level.
B. All bolts tight and secure.
C. Seal is in good condition and not leaking.
questions.explanation: Some hub oil seals will have a plastic or glass area, so you are able to tell that the oil is at the proper level. If there is not an area to view the oil it will still need to be said. It will have several bolts, and they need to be tight and secure. Also, the seal needs to be in good condition and not leaking.

questions.question: Differences between the steer axel and the rest of the axles are: tread depth, spacers or budding rims, space between the tires, torsion bars, and air bags.
questions.explanation: Steer axels are as simple as an axel can get. They only have one tire on each side, so no spacers, space, or bud rims are required. The tread depth is different from any other axel, and it usually does not have a torsion bar or air bags.

questions.question: You can leave the hood open when moving on with the pre-trip.
questions.explanation: Open the hood to do the engine compartment, and close it before walking away. You should never leave the engine compartment with the hood open.

questions.question: After the engine compartment it is best to move to the driver's side of vehicle, and then head into the cab.
questions.explanation: This is true. It is best to get to the inside cab early. If you do not make it to the inside can you can automatically fail for not doing the CDL air brakes test.

questions.question: At the side of the cab you should not check.
questions.explanation: All these items will all appear on your CDL pre-trip. The correct answer is none of these.

questions.question: The fuel and air tanks are checked for the same items except?
questions.explanation: Both the fuel and air tanks should be checked for proper mount, no leaks, and good hoses. Only the fuel tank will have a cap so you may fill the tanks.

questions.question: Steps leading into the vehicle should be?
options: Properly mounted, not damaged, and all bolts tight and secure.
Strong enough to support twice your weight.
questions.explanation: Make sure the steps are properly mounted, no damage, and bolts are present and secure.

questions.question: Handrails should be checked for?
questions.explanation: Handrails will need to be tight and secure, properly mounted, all bolts in place, and no excessive damage.

questions.question: Is it best to check the seat and the seatbelts before sitting down?
questions.explanation: We suggest checking the seat and belt for securement and damage before sitting down. You will be in a hurry, and it is best to mention them when you see them.

questions.question: The first thing you should check or do when you sit in the driver's seat is?
questions.explanation: As soon as you sit in the driver's seat please buckle your seatbelt. If you move the vehicle at all without your seatbelt fastened it is an automatic fail.

questions.question: Check your mirrors from the inside of the cab for?
options: Adjusted so that you can see.
questions.explanation: If you checked them for mounts, cracks, and clean while outside of the vehicle there is no need to state those again. Adjustment can only be checked from the driver's seat, but if you forgot to mention the mirrors on the outside of the vehicle you can check them now for everything.

questions.question: Items inside the cab you must make function in order to get credit for them are?
options: Blower motors, temperature control, and diverter.
questions.explanation: If you just mention the wipers and do not check to make sure they work you will not get credit for them. This is true with all the answers here.

questions.question: The steering wheel should be checked for?
questions.explanation: Steering wheels should not have more than 2" of play or 10 degrees in a 20" wheel.

questions.question: Before you start the vehicle you should check?
questions.explanation: Making sure the vehicle is in neutral, parking brake set, and seat belt on is steps to a safe start of the vehicle. You should also apply the clutch if equipped before starting.

questions.question: These are all gauges that will need checked except?
questions.explanation: We do not check the water pressure gauge, instead you should check the water temperature gauge.

questions.question: The air pressure in a commercial vehicle should rise to governor cutout of?
questions.explanation: Air pressure should rise to between 120-140 PSI.

questions.question: Which gauge should be between 12-14, and in the green?
questions.explanation: The voltmeter should be between 12-14, and in the green to be working properly.

questions.question: What should the water temperature gauge do when you start the vehicle?
options: Nothing, then rise slowly as the vehicle warms up.
questions.explanation: The temperature gauge will more than likely not move until the vehicle starts to warm up.

questions.question: You don't have to make both the air and city horns work to get credit for them.
questions.explanation: You need to make both the air and city horns work to get credit for checking them.

questions.question: What interior lights do you need to check?
options: Left and right turn indicator lights.
questions.explanation: You will need to check and make each light indicator work in order to get credit. While you are checking lights, it might not be a bad idea to check the dome light as well.

questions.question: What items are part of your safety equipment?
questions.explanation: All these items are part of your safety equipment.

questions.question: To test the parking brake you should have the trailer air supply in, trailer hand break released, and the parking brake _____?
questions.explanation: The parking brake will need to be out or engaged to test the parking brake.

questions.question: Testing the parking brake requires you to?
options: Move the vehicle slowly and then apply the parking brake stopping the vehicle.
Pull against the engaged parking brake with no movement.
Pull against the engaged parking brake with some movement.
Move the vehicle quickly and then apply the parking brake stopping the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The vehicle will need to be stopped with parking brake applied, and the trailer air supply pushed in. Put the vehicle in gear and gently pull against the parking brake with no movement.

questions.question: To test the service brake test you will need to have the trailer air supply valve in, parking brake in, and the hand brake released. How do you test the service brake?
options: Pull against the service brake with no movement.
Pull against the service brake with a little movement.
Move quickly and apply the service brake to stop the vehicle.
Move slowly and apply the service brake to stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Moving slowly, less than 5 MPH, and apply the service brake with steady pressure. The vehicle should come to a smooth and even stop with no pull to one side or the other.

questions.question: The next step is the CDL air brake test. This portion is done with the engine off, but should you have air pressure built up to governor cut of 120-140?
questions.explanation: Yes, the pressure should be built up to governor cutoff to ensure you have enough air pressure to complete the CDL air brake test.

questions.question: During the CDL air brakes tests the first step is to check for air leakage?
questions.explanation: It is best to check the air leakage rate first or you will have to rebuild pressure after draining tanks to make sure the trailer air supply and parking brake set on their own.

questions.question: To test air leakage the air valves should be?
options: Trailer air supply in, parking brake in, trolley released, and pressure on brake pedal.
Trailer air supply out, parking brake in, trolley released, and pressure on the brake pedal.
Trailer air supply in, parking brake out, trolley released, and no pressure on the brake pedal.
Trailer air supply in, parking brake in, trolley applied, and pressure on the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To properly test the air leakage you will need trailer air supply in to supply air to the trailer, parking brake in filling the red line with air, steady pressure applied to the brake pedal filling the blue line with air, and the trolley released so no extra air is supplied to the blue line.

questions.question: Step 1 of the CDL air brake tests makes sure the leak rate of the red and blue line is not unsafe. With the parking brake released and the brake pedal applied the leak rate should be no more than?
options: 3 PSI for a vehicle with no trailer, and 3 PSI for a combination vehicle in one minute.
3 PSI for a vehicle with no trailer, and 4 PSI for a combination vehicle in one minute.
2 PSI for a vehicle with no trailer, and 3 PSI for a combination vehicle in one minute.
2 PSI for a vehicle with no trailer, and 2 PSI for the tractor plus 1 PSI for each trailer in a combination vehicle in one minute.
questions.explanation: The air leak rate should be no more than 2 PSI for the red line, 1 PSI for the blue line. In a non- combination vehicle that is 3. For a combination vehicle you will need to add 1 PSI for the trailer bringing the total to 4.

questions.question: Next you should fan the brakes down to make sure all air brake safety devices are working, but what should you do before starting to fan the brakes?
options: Make sure the vehicle is in neutral.
Turn the key on so that the instrument warning lights come on.
questions.explanation: You will need to have the key on to accessory or to the position right before you start the vehicle. This needs to be done so that the alarm and light for the low air warning can come on alerting of low air pressure. If the light and alarm does not come on when you are taking your test you may automatically fail.

questions.question: While fanning down the alarm and light indicating low air pressure should come on at?
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light and alarm should come on when the air pressure is around 60 PSI.

questions.question: Fanning the brakes down further after the alarm and buzzer come on should result in the parking brake popping out for a single vehicle, and the parking brake and the trailer air supply popping out for a combination vehicle at?
questions.explanation: The parking brake for vehicles with no trailer, and the parking brake and trailer air supply valve for combination vehicles should set or pop out at 40 PSI.

questions.question: Before you leave the inside can you should not check the exterior lights.
questions.explanation: It is best to check the lights before getting out, and it will allow the air pressure to build back up if you safely restart the engine.

questions.question: Exterior lights that need checked are on which side of the vehicle?
options: Front of vehicle, rear of vehicle.
Front of vehicle, both sides of vehicle, and rear of vehicle.
Front of vehicle, and both sides.
Answer B plus rear of tractor in combination vehicles.
questions.explanation: Lights will need to be checked on the front, both sides, rear of tractor on combination vehicles, and the rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: What lights will you need to check on the exterior?
options: Hazard, headlights, running, and clearance lights.
Hazard, left turn, right turn, headlights high and low beam, brake, running, and clearance lights.
Left turn, right turn, headlights high and low beam, running, and clearance lights.
Hazard, left turn, right turn, running, and headlights high and low beam.
questions.explanation: You need to check the hazard, left turn, right turn, headlights high and low beam, and the clearance lights. Please remember to check each at the front of the vehicle except brake lights, all but headlights and brake lights on both sides, and all except headlights at the back of the vehicle. If this is a combination vehicle check the rear of the tractor for all except headlights.

questions.question: What should you remember to check while exiting the vehicle?
questions.explanation: Best to make sure you check the handrails, steps, fuel tank, and air tanks at this time.

questions.question: Hand rails and steps should be checked for?
questions.explanation: The handrails and step need to be secure, not damaged, and able to support the weight you are applying to them when entering the vehicle.

questions.question: When you check the Fuel tank you can also say you would check the same items on the air tanks. What should these two items be checked for?
options: Securely mounted, mounting bands and rubber grommets in good condition, lines between the tanks secure with no damage, and no leaks from the tanks or the lines.
Securely mounted, mounting bands in good condition, lines between the tanks secure with no damage, and no leaks from the tanks or the lines.
Securely mounted, mounting bands in good condition, lines between the tanks secure with no damage, and no leaks from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Please make sure that you point at or touch both tanks to insure you receive credit for them, and they both need checked for security, bands and grommets, the lines between tanks, and leaks.

questions.question: You should mention you would check all light covers and reflectors for damage on the side of the vehicle, both the tractor and the trailer, again to cover the side since you have only checked the front at this time?
questions.explanation: This is true, on each side of the vehicle you need to check the light lenses and reflectors, and you should get credit for both the tractor and the trailer if you tell the examiner you would check both at this time. The lenses and reflectors need to be mounted, clean, and not damaged or missing.

questions.question: When checking the air and electrical lines between the tractor and the trailer what should you be checking for?
options: The connection at the tractor, the lines for breaks cracks frays, and the connection to the trailer.
The connection at the tractor, the lines for breaks cracks frays, the connection to the trailer, and that none of these are leaking.
questions.explanation: Make sure to check the connection at the tractor, the lines for breaks cracks frays, the connection to the trailer, and that none of these are leaking. Group them together at the tractor, between the vehicle, and at the trailer to make this part go quickly.

questions.question: What are a few items you want to check while between the tractor and trailer?
options: Frame, catwalk, exhaust, cab mounts, and driveshaft.
Frame, catwalk, exhaust, and cab mounts.
questions.explanation: Frame needs checked for cracks, bends, illegal welds, that it is secure, and mounting bolts. Catwalk needs to be in good condition with all mounting bolts in place. Exhaust needs to be secure; all pipes and connections need to be secure and free of leaks. The driveshaft needs to be properly mounted, tight sand secure, u-joints in good condition and move freely, and there is no excessive play.

questions.question: The rest of the axels on the vehicle are nearly the same as the front steer axels, with a few differences. What are the differences?
options: Torsion bar, space between the tires or spacers, and air bags.
Torsion bar, treads, space between the tires or spacers, and air bags.
Torsion bar, treads, and air bags.
Tread depth, space between the tires or spacers, and air bags.
questions.explanation: There are FOUR differences between the steer axel, and the tractor and trailer axels. They are the Torsion bar, the space between the axels so bud rims or spacers, tread depth changes from four thirty seconds to two thirty seconds, and retreads are allowed on every axel but the steer axel, and the air bags portion of the suspension.

questions.question: The apron is the metal plate welded on the bottom of the trailer that gives the 5th wheel a smooth surface for vehicle connection. What should you check the apron for?
options: That it is not bent, damaged, cracked, and that it is securely mounted.
That it is not bent, and that it is securely mounted.
That it is not bent, damaged, or cracked.
That it is not bent, damaged, or cracked, has no illegal welds, and that it is securely mounted.
questions.explanation: The apron itself should not be bent, cracked, or damaged. It will be welded to the bottom of the trailer, but it should not have welds on the surface that the 5th wheel contacts, and it should be securely mounted.

questions.question: The kingpin is a cylindric piece of metal protruding down from the apron, it has a base which is near the apron, shank or the narrow section of the kingpin where the locking jaws connect, and the head or the part furthest from the apron. What should you check the kingpin for?
options: Not bent or damaged, no cracks, and no illegal welds.
Securely mounted, no cracks, and no illegal welds.
Securely mounted, not bent or damaged, no cracks, and no illegal welds.
Securely mounted, not bent or damaged, and no cracks.
questions.explanation: The kingpin is part of what holds the tractor and trailer together, it needs to be straight with no damage. You should not have any cracks in the metal, and there should not be any welds on the visible portion of the kingpin.

questions.question: The 5th wheel is mounted on the back of the tractor, it lifts the trailer slightly when it contacts the apron when you are coupling the vehicles, and it houses the locking jaws which wrap around the shank of the kingpin to securely attach the trailer. True or False: The 5th wheel should be greased, no illegal welds, not damaged, and tilt with enough pressure.
questions.explanation: This is true. The 5th wheel tilts so that the coupling can withstand unlevel surfaces, it cannot have welds or cracks, and needs to be secure.

questions.question: You should check to make sure that the locking jaws are completely wrapped around the shank of the kingpin during your pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: This is true. The kingpin needs to be completely extended and around the shank of the kingpin.

questions.question: When coupled there should be a slight gap between the 5th wheel and the apron, meaning you should be able to see light between the two.
questions.explanation: To have a properly connected vehicle there can be no gap between the 5th wheel and the apron. If there is a gap you should disconnect the tractor, lower the front of trailer, and recouple the tractor. A gap could mean the locking jaws went around the head of the kingpin instead of the shank. This is dangerous because a large bump may cause the trailer to lift, and the kingpin to slide out of the locking jaws.

questions.question: The 5th wheel has a release arm built into the side of it, it automatically locks the jaws around the kingpin when you connect the vehicles, but it can be pulled out to release the locking jaws for uncoupling. What is the correct position of the release arm when the vehicle is coupled?
options: completely in with the locking mechanism secured.
completely out with the locking mechanism secured.
completely in with the locking mechanism released.
completely out with the locking mechanism released.
questions.explanation: The release arm needs to be pushed completely in with the locking mechanism secured. You want to make sure this is secure because if it is not the trailer might break free of the locking jaws.

questions.question: Most 5th wheels are adjustable for weight distribution and turn clearance, these are called sliding 5th wheels, they have a release are that needs to be completely in and locked, and a locking mechanism. What locks the 5th wheel in place?
questions.explanation: Locking pins extend through holes in the platform to lock the sliding 5th wheel in place.

questions.question: The 5th wheel platform needs to be checked for?
options: Tight and secure, properly mounted, and there are no illegal welds.
Tight and secure, all the bolts are in place and secure, and there are no illegal welds.
Tight and secure, properly mounted, all the bolts are in place and secure, not excessively damaged, and there are no illegal welds.
Tight and secure, properly mounted, and all the bolts are in place and secure.
questions.explanation: The platform needs to be free of illegal welds, be tight and secure, properly mounted, not damaged, and all bolts need to be in place and secure.

questions.question: At the rear of the tractor there are still a few things to check, what are they?
options: ICC bumper, mud flaps, light lens covers, and reflectors.
Mud flaps, light lens covers, and reflectors.
Air lines, ICC bumper, and reflectors.
Mud flaps, air lines, and ICC bumper.
questions.explanation: The only things you needed to check at the rear of the tractor are the light lens covers, reflectors, and the mud flaps.
